item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies Included under Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme
Government of India approves the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC) proposal to include the Chemicals and Petrochemicals under RDI Scheme
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has included Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies as an additional technology area eligible for funding under the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, with effect from 8 October 2026.

The decision has been taken by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, following a proposal by the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC), Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.

DCPC had proposed the inclusion of the chemicals and petrochemicals sector as a priority area under the RDI Scheme. The decision is expected to strengthen research, development and innovation in the chemicals and petrochemicals sector and facilitate the development of indigenous technologies for advanced industrial applications.

Under the visionary leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India launched the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme in November 2025, with a corpus of ₹1 lakh crore to catalyse private-sector investment in research, development and innovation. The scheme seeks to provide long-term financing and refinancing on favourable terms for transformative projects, accelerate the adoption of advanced technologies, strengthen India’s industrial competitiveness and foster self-reliance in critical and emerging technology areas.

At the launch of the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme last year, the Prime Minister said, “India is rapidly building a vibrant ecosystem for research and development. We are focusing on Ease of Doing Research so that a modern ecosystem of innovation can flourish in India.”

Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilizers & Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, has welcomed the inclusion of the sector under the RDI Scheme and described it as an important development for the chemicals and petrochemicals industry.

Shri Nadda said the decision would provide a much-needed impetus to research and innovation, supporting the development of advanced, efficient and cost-effective technologies for manufacturing chemicals, petrochemical products, polymers and their derivatives in India.

The inclusion of Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies is aligned with the broader objective of strengthening India's domestic manufacturing ecosystem, promoting technology-led industrial growth and reducing dependence on imported technologies and high-value materials.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
NCISM Chairperson launches CCRAS SPARK 5.0 and CCRAS Ayurshodh 2026 to strengthen Ayurveda research and innovation
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Chairperson of National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), Prof. Maneesha Kothekar, today launched CCRAS SPARK 5.0 and CCRAS Ayurshodh 2026 (2nd circular) of the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS). The initiatives aim to strengthen the research ecosystem in Ayurveda by encouraging research among undergraduate students and recognising scholarly excellence, research communication and innovation.

CCRAS SPARK 5.0

The Studentship Program for Ayurveda Research Ken (SPARK) 5.0 for 2026-27 is the fifth edition of the programme. It seeks to introduce undergraduate Ayurveda students to research methodology and techniques through short-term independent research projects, and to foster research aptitude, analytical thinking and early interest in research as a career among BAMS students.

  • A total of 300 studentships are being offered, with a studentship amount of ₹50,000.
  • BAMS students in their third/fourth/professional years studying in NCISM/Government of India-recognised colleges or universities are eligible.
  • Registration opens on 15 October 2026. The last date for submission of applications is 15 November 2026.

CCRAS Ayurshodh – National Research Recognitions

CCRAS Ayurshodh provides a platform to recognise and encourage research contributions in Ayurveda across three categories:

  • CCRAS-Prabodh 3MT: Communication of research through three-minute thesis presentations.
  • CCRAS-Prakash: Recognition of scholarly achievements through publications based on original research.
  • CCRAS-Navonmesha: Recognition of innovative prototypes, novel solutions, process innovations and transformative research methodologies.

The second circular details the awards, including prize money sponsored by Shree Dhootapapeshwar Limited. The finals of CCRAS Ayurshodh are scheduled for 11 December 2026.

Prof. (Vaidya) Rabinarayan Acharya, Director General, CCRAS; Dr. Ranjit Puranik, MD and CEO, Shree Dhootapapeshwar Limited; Presidents of various NCISM boards and heads of CCRAS institutes across the country were present on the occasion.

The initiatives are intended to nurture emerging research talent, promote effective research communication, encourage quality scholarly publications and foster innovative approaches to advancing Ayurveda research.

Further information is available at the following links:

  • CCRAS SPARK 5.0: https://spark.ccras.org.in/
  • CCRAS Ayurshodh: https://ayurshodh.ccras.org.in/

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Government mobilizes National Law Universities to target Criminal Case Backlogs across 100 Hotspot Districts
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:43PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant move to address the issue of pendency of cases at the District and Subordinate Judiciary, the Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India, has decided to take action in a focused manner by identifying hotspot districts where such cases are in large number. Accordingly, under the guidance of Union Law Minister Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, the department has initiated a nationwide, research-based mission targeting the top 100 judicial districts with high litigation pendency. Over 5.8 crore cases are pending across courts in the country, of which the majority are in district and subordinate courts. Further, those identified  100 districts account for over half of all district-court pendency.

Accordingly, under this initiative, a meeting was convened with Vice Chancellors of nineteen National Law Universities of sixteen states. The meeting was convened through video conferencing. It was  chaired by the Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal.

Secretary, Department of Justice, the Director General (Awards), the Director General, Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D), the Director General, National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), and other officials attended the meeting physically. 

During the discussions, various alternatives like identifying infructuous cases, case profiling, alternative dispute resolution, management of adjournments, plea bargaining, mediation assisted settlements, bringing summary trial process etc. were deliberated upon. It was also highlighted to the NLUs that they may effectively utilize their pro bono clubs, researchers and students to carry out the ground level analysis  of case pendency in the selected districts and suggest possible strategies to address the issue. As the way forward, NLUs were requested to develop focused approach for the 100 districts, based on district-specific diagnosis and identify the main causes of delay. They were also requested to suggest feasible mechanism to reduce litigation pendency. All the Vice Chancellors of NLUs have assured their active participation and their willingness to serve the Nation.

Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal summed up by reiterating the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji for Viksit Bharat @2047, for which an accessible, efficient, cost effective, fair, speedy and responsive justice delivery system is essential.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
ITRA, Jamnagar to Organise National Symposium ‘Ayutech Navonmesh 2026’ on Artificial Intelligence in Ayurveda
Two-day event on October 15–16 to explore the integration of traditional Ayurvedic knowledge with modern digital technologies on the occasion of the Institute’s Sixth Foundation Day
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, under the Ministry of Ayush, will organise the Dr. P. M. Mehta Oration and the two-day national symposium ‘Ayutech Navonmesh 2026’ on October 15 and 16, 2026, to mark the Institute’s Sixth Foundation Day. The central theme of the symposium is ‘Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Ayurveda’. The event aims to explore opportunities for advancing research, innovation and healthcare services through the integration of traditional Ayurvedic knowledge with modern digital technologies.

The programme will be held under the leadership of Prof. (Dr.) Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA. Hon’ble Member of Parliament Smt. Poonamben Madam will attend as the Chief Guest. Mr. Sameer Pujari, Head of Data, Digital Health, Analytics and Artificial Intelligence in the Division of Health Systems at the World Health Organization (WHO), Switzerland, and Dr. Shyama Kuruvilla, Director of the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre, will also participate in the event. Distinguished guests will include Prof. Shailendra Saraf, Director, National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER), Gandhinagar; Dr. Mansi Deshpande, Vice-Chancellor, Gujarat Ayurved University; and Dr. Manoj Nesari, former Adviser (Ayurveda), Ministry of Ayush.

The participation of these eminent experts is expected to facilitate meaningful deliberations on the convergence of Ayurveda and modern digital technologies, with a focus on research and innovation. National and international experts will discuss the potential applications of artificial intelligence and digital technologies in Ayurvedic research, drug development, education and healthcare delivery.

The symposium will feature expert lectures, academic discussions, deliberations on research and technological collaboration, institutional recognitions and cultural programmes. Special emphasis will be placed on the ethical, scientific and practical applications of AI in Ayurvedic research, drug development, quality assurance, medical education and healthcare services.

Prof. (Dr.) Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA, said that the integration of Ayurveda and artificial intelligence could open up new avenues for research and innovation. She emphasised that connecting traditional knowledge with modern scientific and data-driven approaches could contribute meaningfully to the advancement of Ayurveda, knowledge exchange and the strengthening of public healthcare services.

Through this initiative, ITRA, Jamnagar, aims to provide a common platform for Ayurveda scholars, researchers, practitioners and technology experts, while promoting responsible technological innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration in traditional medicine.

About ITRA, Jamnagar

Dedicated to the nation by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on October 15, 2020, ITRA is the first institution in the country to receive the status of an Institution of National Importance in the field of Ayurveda. Located in Jamnagar, a city renowned for its historical and academic traditions in Ayurveda, the Institute promotes education and research through programmes ranging from undergraduate to doctoral levels, along with courses related to Ayurveda pharmacy, yoga and naturopathy.

The Institute operates a 300-bed hospital accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH), where an average of approximately 1,000 patients receive treatment daily through the Outpatient Department (OPD). Since its establishment, the Institute has provided consultation and treatment to a total of 18,47,807 patients through its OPD, while 27,520 patients have received inpatient care. Currently, 20 OPDs are functioning across various departments of the Institute. In addition, weekly OPD services are provided at eight locations across Jamnagar city and district.

The Institute also houses six laboratories accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), equipped with modern scientific instruments, along with dedicated facilities for yoga and naturopathy.

In the fields of education and research, ITRA has signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with 27 institutions, including 18 national and nine international institutions. Its Ayurveda library houses more than 30,000 books and over 5,000 manuscripts. The Institute also maintains an animal house facility for medical and pharmaceutical research in accordance with prescribed standards.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
KAUMARACON 2026 to Begin at AIIA, New Delhi, on October 15; Vice-President to Address International Ayurveda Paediatrics Conference
Three-Day Conference from October 15–17 to Bring Together National and International Experts in Child Healthcare
AIIA to Celebrate Foundation Day on October 17
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi

The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, will organise KAUMARACON 2026, the International Conference on Kaumarabhritya (Ayurveda Paediatrics), from October 15 to 17, 2026, at its Sarita Vihar campus in New Delhi.

The three-day conference will bring together experts, academicians, researchers, practitioners and students from India and abroad to deliberate on advancements in Ayurveda-based child healthcare, research and clinical practice.

The inaugural session on October 15 will be attended by the Hon’ble Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, as the Chief Guest. Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, and Minister of State, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, will attend as the Guest of Honour. Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, and Dr. Maneesha Upendra Kothekar, Chairperson, National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), will also be present.

Highlighting the Institute’s journey and achievements, Prof. (Vaidya) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, said that the Institute, conceptualised in 2002 and dedicated to the nation by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in 2017, is entering its tenth year. He noted that AIIA has made significant progress in Ayurveda education, patient care and research. AIIA, New Delhi, has more than 200 inpatient beds and advanced diagnostic facilities, while the establishment of AIIA Goa in 2022 has further expanded its institutional reach. He added that KAUMARACON 2026 reflects the Institute’s commitment to advancing specialised Ayurveda healthcare, particularly in the field of child health.

AIIA is affiliated with the University of Delhi for postgraduate education and PhD research programmes and has received NAAC A++ accreditation. Its hospital is accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH). The Institute undertakes academic, intramural, extramural and industry-sponsored research projects and publishes three research journals.

Kaumarabhritya: Advancing Comprehensive Child Healthcare

Kaumarabhritya is a specialised branch of Ayurveda that focuses on child health and well-being, including growth and development, nutrition, immunity, mental health and the management of childhood diseases.

The Department of Kaumarabhritya at AIIA provides outpatient and inpatient services, newborn care through a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), vaccination, mental healthcare and skin care. The department also operates a specialised outpatient service for cancer care in children and attends to approximately 120–150 children daily in its outpatient section.

The department has established the KINDER Lab (Kaumarabhritya Initiative for Neurology, Dermatology, Respiratory and related areas), a specialised diagnostic facility supporting clinical assessment and research in paediatric healthcare.

Prof. Dr. Rajagopala S., Head of the Department of Kaumarabhritya, AIIA, and Organising Chairman of KAUMARACON 2026, said that children’s health and well-being are fundamental to building a healthy society. He emphasised that Kaumarabhritya addresses the comprehensive healthcare needs of children, from nutrition and immunity to physical growth, mental well-being and disease management. He added that the conference would facilitate scientific exchange, dissemination of research findings and collaboration among professionals working in Ayurveda paediatrics.

The third edition of KAUMARACON follows the conferences held in 2019 and 2023 at Ayurveda University, Jodhpur, Rajasthan. The 2026 edition is expected to attract more than 500 participants, including experts, teachers, practitioners, postgraduate scholars and students from across the country. International experts from Brazil, the United States, Germany, Sri Lanka and Nepal are also expected to participate online.

The scientific programme will include a pre-conference workshop on computer-aided drug designing (Ayurinformatics) and diagnostics in paediatrics, an oration lecture, six scientific sessions, including a session with international experts, and 12 parallel sessions.

More than 175 scientific papers are scheduled to be presented during the conference. The deliberations will provide a platform for sharing research outcomes, clinical experiences and innovative approaches in Ayurveda paediatrics. The conference aims to promote evidence-based scientific dialogue, encourage interdisciplinary collaboration and strengthen the role of Ayurveda in comprehensive child healthcare.

The three-day programme will culminate on October 17 with the Foundation Day celebrations of the All India Institute of Ayurveda, commemorating the Institute’s establishment, institutional growth and contributions to Ayurveda education, healthcare and research.

The Foundation Day programme will highlight the Institute’s achievements in academic excellence, patient care, research and the development of specialised healthcare services. Faculty members, students, researchers, practitioners and invited guests are expected to participate in the celebrations.

Through KAUMARACON 2026 and its Foundation Day celebrations, AIIA seeks to promote specialised paediatric healthcare, strengthen scientific research and foster knowledge exchange, while advancing Ayurveda’s contribution to the country’s healthcare system.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India and Brunei Darussalam Review Bilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation at Third Joint Trade Committee Meeting
Discussions Focus on Expanding Bilateral Trade, Improving Market Access and Facilitating Business-to-Business Exchanges
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:30PM by PIB Delhi

The third meeting of the India–Brunei Darussalam Joint Trade Committee (JTC) was convened to review bilateral trade and economic cooperation and identify avenues for strengthening commercial ties between the two countries. The meeting was co-chaired by Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, India, Shri Amit Verma, and Permanent Secretary (Economy & Trade), Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Brunei Darussalam, Dr. May Fa'ezah Ahmad Ariffin. Representatives from relevant Ministries, Departments and organisations of both countries participated in the deliberations.

The discussions focused on expanding bilateral trade, addressing market access priorities and identifying institutional mechanisms to facilitate business-to-business exchanges. Both sides also deliberated on facilitating exports of agricultural and animal products from India to Brunei Darussalam, with a view to supporting food security and diversifying trade.

Pharmaceuticals, healthcare and energy were identified as key areas for further cooperation. Both sides explored opportunities for regulatory collaboration, procurement and healthcare services, recognising the potential for greater engagement in the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors. Discussions on energy covered traditional and emerging energy partnerships to support sustained industrial growth.

The two sides also emphasised the importance of strengthening people-to-people ties and commercial outreach through cooperation in tourism and participation in trade fairs and exhibitions. They noted that targeted trade promotion events and reciprocal business delegations could help identify investment opportunities in manufacturing, infrastructure and services.

Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining regular communication between relevant nodal agencies and working groups to monitor follow-up actions and advance the trade and investment objectives discussed during the meeting.

The next meeting of the India–Brunei Darussalam Joint Trade Committee will be held in Brunei Darussalam.

***

Abhishek Dayal/Garima Singh/Anushka Pandey

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Close defence-academia-industry collaboration key to accelerating development & adoption of indigenous tech amid evolving nature of warfare: Raksha Mantri
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called for close collaboration among the Defence Forces, DRDO, academic institutions, defence public sector undertakings and private industry, including start-ups, to accelerate the development, adoption & continuous upgradation of indigenous technologies amidst the rapidly evolving nature of warfare. Speaking at the launch of IIT Kanpur’s ‘Greater Than Us’ fundraising campaign in New Delhi on October 14, 2026, he emphasised that strengthening indigenous technological capabilities is strategically crucial as artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, unmanned platforms, advanced sensors, cybersecurity and space-based technologies are reshaping military dynamics.

Raksha Mantri underscored the growing interlinkage between national security and technological capability, stressing that IITs can make a significant contribution by aligning academic research with operational defence requirements and industry needs. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi-led Government’s ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ commitment lies at the centre of its ‘Viksit Bharat’ vision as it aims to create a technologically capable, economically competitive, innovative and confident nation, which is not just a consumer of knowledge & technology but an active contributor to their creation, he said.

Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted the importance of strong institutions of higher education and research in realising this vision, noting that the Government has made sustained efforts to strengthen the ecosystem, whose growing contribution to innovation and entrepreneurship is reflected in the IIT ecosystem’s support for over 6,000 start-ups, 56 unicorns and nearly 5,000 patents. “These achievements demonstrate that IITs are not merely institutions that impart knowledge, but are increasingly becoming engines of innovation, enterprise and technological capability. Institutions such as IIT Kanpur play a significant role in advancing India’s development by expanding scientific capabilities, strengthening the innovation ecosystem and creating solutions that benefit society,” he added.

Acknowledging the initiatives undertaken in this direction, Raksha Mantri made special mention of IIT Kanpur’s DRDO-Industry-Academia Centre of Excellence and welcomed the proposal to establish a School of Defence Technologies at the Institute. He added that the proposal to set up a National Military Drone Technology Hub at IIT Kanpur, in collaboration with the Ministry of Defence to fast-track indigenisation and innovation to gain combat edge, has made significant progress and its approval process is nearing completion. 

Shri Rajnath Singh exuded confidence that such partnerships would bring scientific talent, institutional expertise and the operational experience of the Defence Forces under one umbrella to develop indigenous technologies of strategic importance. Credible academic institutions can play a crucial role in translating research into practical defence applications and addressing the evolving technological requirements of the military, he said.

On IIT Kanpur’s role in strengthening Uttar Pradesh’s industrial ecosystem, Raksha Mantri said that the institute can serve as a bridge between scientific research and industrial application, emerging technologies and enterprise. He noted that Kanpur’s rich industrial legacy, coupled with IIT Kanpur’s technological expertise can generate new opportunities for entrepreneurship, employment, investment and economic growth, contributing to the state’s vision of becoming a one-trillion-dollar economy.

Shri Rajnath Singh referred to the C3i Cybersecurity Technology Innovation Hub at IIT Kanpur and the institute’s medical school, terming them as significant initiatives in cybersecurity, healthcare and medical technology innovation. He stated that research in emerging areas such as advanced materials, semiconductors, quantum technology and environmental sustainability would be critical to addressing national priorities and developing future technologies.

Stressing the need for sustained investment in research and innovation, Raksha Mantri referred to the Government’s approval of Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation Scheme to catalyse private-sector investment in research & advanced technologies. “While public policy can create an enabling environment, institutions must nurture talent and generate ideas, and industry must help translate innovations into practical applications and scale them up,” he said.

Through the ‘Greater Than Us’ campaign, IIT Kanpur aims to raise US$1 billion by March 2029, which is the largest fundraising campaign ever undertaken by any IIT. Rs 4,155 crore, nearly half of the goal, has already been committed by alumni, donors, corporate partners, and the government. The objective is to strengthen IIT Kanpur’s research infrastructure, nurture talent, and accelerate the development and commercialisation of indigenous technologies & innovations to support India’s vision of becoming a developed nation by 2047.

Shri Rajnath Singh expressed confidence that the campaign would support stronger research capabilities, advanced facilities, opportunities for talented students and solutions to national & global challenges. He called upon the institute’s alumni, industry, philanthropic supporters and institutional partners to contribute through financial support, mentorship, research partnerships and professional networks. 

Prof Manindra Agrawal, Director, IIT Kanpur; Shri Awanish Kumar Awasthi, Advisor to the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh and faculty, students & alumni of the institute were present on the occasion.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
India Strengthens Science and Technology Partnerships with Global South through Inaugural Ministry of External Affairs–CSIR Tech Familiarization Programme
33 Ambassadors and Embassy Officials from 29 Countries Explore CSIR's Innovations in Sustainable Infrastructure, Genomics and Healthcare
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 7:55PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant initiative to strengthen India's science and technology partnerships with countries of the Global South, the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), in collaboration with the New, Emerging and Strategic Technologies (NEST) Division of the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Government of India, launched the inaugural edition of the MEA–CSIR Tech Familiarization Programme on 14 October 2026.

The programme brought together 33 Ambassadors and senior embassy officials representing 29 countries, providing them with first-hand exposure to CSIR's scientific capabilities, indigenous technologies and advanced research infrastructure. The inaugural edition featured visits to two premier CSIR laboratories in New Delhi—the CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI) and the CSIR-Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology (CSIR-IGIB).

Jointly conceptualised by CSIR and MEA, the initiative seeks to build stronger scientific and technological linkages with partner countries, particularly across the Global South, by showcasing India's research capabilities and identifying opportunities for collaborative research, technology transfer, capacity building and deployment of innovative solutions addressing shared developmental challenges.

During the inaugural session, Dr. Rama Swami Bansal, Head, International S&T Affairs Directorate, CSIR, presented an overview of CSIR's scientific and technological capabilities, its international engagements and potential models for collaboration with countries of the Global South. Dr. Sadre Alam, Joint Secretary, MEA, outlined the genesis, objectives and expectations of the programme, highlighting its role in fostering international partnerships through science and technology.

Dr. Chalumuri Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR-CRRI, and Dr. Souvik Maiti, Director, CSIR-IGIB, introduced the visiting delegation to their respective institutes' research strengths, technological achievements and contributions in the areas of sustainable infrastructure and healthcare.

At CSIR-CRRI, the delegation witnessed several advanced research facilities and technologies, including the Driving Simulator, Cyclic Load Test Facility, Steel Slag Laboratory, a 3D model of bio-binder technology and drone models. A major highlight was the live demonstration of Ecofix, a steel slag-based instant pothole repair mix developed for rapid road maintenance. The demonstration showcased how indigenous technologies can transform industrial waste into valuable resources while offering practical, sustainable and cost-effective solutions for infrastructure development.

The delegation subsequently visited CSIR-IGIB, where participants were introduced to advanced facilities in genome sequencing, biosafety, zebrafish research, biobanking and Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP). The visit offered insights into India's growing capabilities in genomics, biomedical research, precision healthcare and biotechnology, highlighting opportunities for scientific cooperation and capacity building in the healthcare sector.

The programme concluded with an interactive session during which the visiting Ambassadors and embassy officials shared their perspectives, priorities and expectations for future engagement with CSIR. Discussions explored opportunities for joint research, technology partnerships, knowledge exchange, capacity building and adaptation of Indian technologies to address the specific developmental needs of partner countries.

The inaugural MEA–CSIR Tech Familiarization Programme represents an important step towards translating India's scientific and technological strengths into meaningful international partnerships. By bringing foreign diplomatic representatives directly into CSIR laboratories and facilitating interactions with scientists and technology developers, the initiative provides a platform for identifying practical areas of cooperation and accelerating the adoption of innovative solutions.

The programme is expected to open new avenues for sustained engagement between CSIR and countries of the Global South, reinforcing India's commitment to sharing scientific knowledge, technological expertise and indigenous innovations for inclusive and sustainable development.

Ministry of Defence
Defence Accounts Department Organises Shramdaan under ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’ Campaign
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Defence Accounts Department organised a nationwide Shramdaan under the ‘Swachhata Hi Seva 2026’ campaign, with field offices participating in the two-week-long Swachhata Pakhwada and planting over 25,000 trees under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative.

The campaign concluded with a cleanliness drive at MCD Primary School, Bagdola, Dwarka, New Delhi, led by Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) Smt Alka Nangia Arora, in association with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi. Officers and staff of the CGDA office and MCD officials participated in the drive, which also included sapling plantation.

As part of Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0, the CGDA Headquarters undertook a tree plantation drive on October 12, 2026. The Department also initiated exercises to identify physical files for weeding out, e-files for closure, scrap and e-waste for disposal.

The nationwide initiatives reaffirm the Defence Accounts Department’s commitment to cleanliness, environmental conservation, responsible waste management and the principles of ‘Reduce, Reuse and Recycle’ through collective participation and Jan Bhagidari.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
MCL commits ₹22.64 Crore for Five CSR projects in Sundargarh District
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 7:42PM by PIB Delhi

Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), under its CSR initiative has signed MoUs with the District Administration of Sundargarh on tuesday for five developmental projects worth ₹22.64 crore. The projects include the rejuvenation and beautification of Kata Bandha (₹4.32 crore), Brahamani Bandha (₹3.98 crore) and Abdul Hussain Bandha (₹2.69 crore); freshwater inland aquaculture in mining-affected areas of Hemgir Block (₹3.81 crore); and renovation, improvement and construction of tanks under Talsara Assembly Constituency (₹7.84 crore) in Sundargarh district.

The General Manager (CSR), MCL, and the District Collector, Sundargarh, signed the MoUs for project implementation by the District Administration.

Aligned with the “Amrit Sarovar” mission, the rejuvenation of water bodies will promote water conservation, groundwater replenishment and environmental improvement while developing leisure destinations, supporting small-scale tourism and generating local economic activity. The works include embankment protection, construction of pathways, bathing steps, stone packing, railings, seating spaces, electrical works and horticulture, aligning with Mission Amrit Sarovar.

The aquaculture project will be implemented in-line with the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana which will benefit over 700 small-scale farmers and FPO members through the development of 50 new ponds and renovation of 20 existing ponds. Besides this, it also includes formation of women-led fish seed production units and Custom Hiring Centres, an Aqua Business School and a Fish Farmers Producers' Organisation (FFPO).

Through these initiatives, MCL aims to strengthen water resource management, promote sustainable livelihoods, support women-led enterprises and contribute to the socio-economic development of communities across Sundargarh district of Odisha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Release of 121st Issue of Sarvekshana, Journal of Official Statistics
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 7:04PM by PIB Delhi

The 121st Issue of Sarvekshana, the premier bi-annual Journal of Official Statistics was released by National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA), Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

Sarvekshana serves as a prominent platform for disseminating research based on data from National Sample Survey (NSS) and other Official Statistics. Recognised for its academic rigour and policy relevance, the journal contributes to the advancement of statistical research and promotes the wider use of official statistical data. It is circulated among researchers, data users, Ministries/Departments, and reputed national and international institutions.

  The 121st Issue features three technical papers, addressing diverse and significant aspects of Official Statistics, namely :-

  1. Impact of In-kind Social Transfer on Level of Living of Indian Households.
  2. Role of Size of Factories in Efficiency – A Study Based on Data from Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) 2022–23.
  3. Effect of Adopting PPS Circular Systematic Sampling in Annual Survey of Industries: A Simulation Study.

  Each paper has undergone a rigorous peer-review and editorial process to ensure its quality, accuracy, and relevance. The studies contribute to a deeper understanding of statistical methodologies, industrial efficiency and the role of social transfers in shaping household living standards.

  In addition to the technical papers, the Issue presents highlights of two Surveys conducted by the NSS, viz. the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) 2025 (January–December 2025) and the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2025 (January–December 2025). The inclusion of these highlights provides readers with key insights into the unincorporated sector and labour market trends, further enhancing the issue's relevance for researchers, policymakers, and other users of official statistics.

  Through the continued publication of Sarvekshana, NSSTA reaffirms its commitment to fostering research in Official Statistics, encouraging the wider application of statistical data, and strengthening the analytical foundations of evidence-based policymaking. The Journal remains an important medium for sharing statistical knowledge, promoting methodological innovation, and supporting informed decision-making.

The Issue can be readily accessed on the websites (www.mospi.gov.in) and NSSTA (www.nssta.gov.in).

Foreign Minister of Canada, H.E. Ms. Anita Anand, called on Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today.

During the meeting, Prime Minister Modi and Foreign Minister Anand discussed ongoing efforts to strengthen bilateral ties and expand cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade, science and technology, defence, security, energy, education, people-to-people ties and multilateral cooperation.

Prime Minister emphasised the importance of sustaining the momentum in bilateral engagement and translating it into tangible outcomes, including through early conclusion of negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). 

They also exchanged views on regional and global developments of mutual interest.

Prime Minister conveyed his warm greetings to Prime Minister Carney and said that he looked forward to continuing their engagements.

item.title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Felicitates 62 Young Innovators at 12th NLEPC, Says School Students Are Turning Ideas into Marketable Products and Entrepreneurship
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology
item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Felicitates 62 Young Innovators at 12th NLEPC, Says School Students Are Turning Ideas into Marketable Products and Entrepreneurship 25 students have already taken products to market; some are earning lakhs while still in school: Dr. Jitendra Singh Union Minister calls for industry partnerships, business-to-business interactions and stronger mentorship to take student innovations to market Around 250 intellectual property rights generated by young innovators; Minister proposes dedicated sessions involving parents INSPIRE-MANAK…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Felicitates 62 Young Innovators at 12th NLEPC, Says School Students Are Turning Ideas into Marketable Products and Entrepreneurship
25 students have already taken products to market; some are earning lakhs while still in school: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Union Minister calls for industry partnerships, business-to-business interactions and stronger mentorship to take student innovations to market
Around 250 intellectual property rights generated by young innovators; Minister proposes dedicated sessions involving parents
INSPIRE-MANAK has selected over 18.27 lakh students since inception in 2009; Compendium released at the ceremony
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 6:38PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today felicitated 62 young innovators at the 12th National Level Exhibition and Project Competition (NLEPC) under INSPIRE-MANAK, saying that school students are increasingly translating their ideas into marketable products and entrepreneurial ventures.

The Minister said 25 students had already taken their products to market, while around 250 intellectual property rights had been generated by young innovators. Some students, he said, were earning lakhs of rupees while still in school, demonstrating how scientific curiosity, commitment and access to opportunities can transform ideas into practical outcomes.

The felicitation ceremony was organised by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, in collaboration with the National Innovation Foundation–India (NIF), at New Delhi. A total of 729 students participated in the event. The ceremony was attended by Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology; Prof. Anil D. Sahasrabudhe, Chairperson, National Innovation Foundation–India; Dr. Umesh Kumar Sharma, Head, Science and Technology Capacity Building Division, DST; and Dr. Arvind C. Ranade, Director, National Innovation Foundation–India, along with senior officials, teachers, mentors and other stakeholders. The INSPIRE-MANAK 2026 Compendium was also released on the occasion.

Interacting with the young innovators, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the students were the main attraction of the programme and that their work had demonstrated the true value of INSPIRE-MANAK. Recalling his initial scepticism about the programme’s name when it was introduced, he said the achievements of the participating students had convinced him of its significance and the high standards of innovation it was fostering.

The Minister referred to several projects presented at the exhibition that addressed everyday challenges through scientific and technological solutions. These included an AI-based alcohol detection system designed to prevent a vehicle from starting when alcohol is detected, an ultrasonic washing machine that can save water, a device designed to deter stray dogs through vibrations, and assistive technology for visually impaired students. He also referred to a tracking walking stick showcased at the exhibition.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the projects demonstrated how students from Classes VI to XII, representing different parts of the country, were identifying problems around them and developing solutions with wider applications. The achievements of students who had taken products to market and secured intellectual property rights reflected the potential to progress from school-level innovation to entrepreneurship and commercial application.

Referring to India’s expanding start-up ecosystem, the Minister said the country’s start-up numbers had grown from around 350–400 in 2014 to approximately 2.5 lakh, with nearly 60 per cent located in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. He said young people today had greater access to information and opportunities, and could achieve significant outcomes through passion, commitment and hard work.

Dr. Jitendra Singh called for stronger industry partnerships to help promising student innovators improve their products, respond to market requirements and explore commercial opportunities. He suggested facilitating business-to-business interactions for young innovators so that their ideas could receive industry feedback and potentially progress towards wider application.

The Minister said promising innovations should not remain confined to exhibitions or working models. Students with entrepreneurial potential should receive opportunities to engage with industry and develop solutions that meet practical needs. He encouraged stakeholders to explore ways of connecting young innovators with relevant enterprises and technical expertise at an early stage.

Citing the example of a policy change that removed the three-year existence requirement for deep-tech start-ups supported by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), Dr. Jitendra Singh said innovation required a willingness to support new ideas and take calculated risks. He called for greater collaboration between the Government and industry to nurture student innovators and help them develop their technologies.

The Minister also stressed the importance of mentorship in enabling students to recognise their strengths, refine their ideas and navigate the journey from an initial concept to a practical application. He proposed that a future edition of the programme include a dedicated session in which young innovators could speak directly about their work and experiences.

Dr. Jitendra Singh proposed that future editions of the programme include a dedicated session in which each participating student is accompanied by at least one parent or guardian. He said parents may sometimes be unfamiliar with the nature of a child’s innovative work and, without intending to discourage them, may inadvertently interrupt the time and effort required to pursue an idea.

The Minister emphasised that parents, teachers and mentors all have an important role in creating an environment where children feel encouraged to experiment, question established approaches and learn from failure. He also stressed the need for students to understand their own capabilities, seek appropriate guidance and remain open to learning as technology and opportunities continue to evolve.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said young innovators must continue developing their skills and adapting to new knowledge rather than becoming complacent after an achievement. He encouraged them to explore their interests, make informed choices and keep improving their ideas through experimentation and practical experience.

Speaking at the event, Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology, said the exhibition reflected the ability of young students to identify problems faced by society and consider how science could help address them. He referred to the geographical diversity of participants, from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to Kashmir and from Mizoram to Mumbai, as well as the variety of projects covering agriculture, healthcare, environmental protection, accessibility, energy, water conservation, safety and improving everyday life for older people.

INSPIRE-MANAK, which stands for Million Minds Augmenting National Aspirations and Knowledge, is a flagship initiative of the Department of Science and Technology implemented in collaboration with the National Innovation Foundation–India, an autonomous body under DST. The programme encourages students from Classes VI to XII to develop original ideas and innovations rooted in science and societal applications.

Since its inception in 2017 a total of 18,27,580 students have been selected under INSPIRE-MANAK up to 2025–26. The Department has organised 11 National Level Exhibition and Project Competitions, at which 7,444 students exhibited their innovative projects and models.

During 2023–24 and 2024–25, 46,926 and 50,009 students, respectively, were selected under the scheme. The 12th NLEPC brought together students selected during these two financial years, providing a national platform to showcase their projects, interact with experts and receive exposure and mentorship.

Under the programme, selected students are supported in developing their ideas into models and proof-of-concept prototypes, with opportunities to improve their projects through workshops and interaction with experts and leading technical institutions. The initiative aims to nurture scientific temper, creativity and innovation from an early age and encourage students to turn observations of everyday challenges into practical solutions.

Congratulating the young innovators, Dr. Jitendra Singh encouraged them to continue questioning, experimenting and learning, and to pursue opportunities to develop their ideas further. He said that supporting young innovators from the school level would help strengthen India’s innovation ecosystem and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat.

****

item.content:encoded:
Cabinet
Government Approves Strategic Restructuring of IDBI Bank Ltd.
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

IDBI Bank Ltd. is a scheduled commercial bank regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Due to its poor financial health, the Bank required repeated infusion of capital, initially provided by the Government of India and later by the LIC. On 5th May, 2017, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) put the IDBI Bank under the Prompt Corrective Action Framework and imposed several restrictions in view of its non-performing assets and losses incurred by the Bank. After considering the improvement in the Bank’s financial health, the RBI later, vide its letter dated 10th March, 2021, lifted the restrictions imposed on the IDBI Bank subject to certain conditions and continuous monitoring.

It was against this backdrop that the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved strategic restructuring of the IDBI Bank Ltd., and in compliance thereof, it was decided that an aggregate 60.72% of the equity stake in the IDBI Bank Ltd be sold to a Strategic Buyer, of which, the GoI share would be 30.48% and the LIC share would be 30.24%, leaving a residual shareholding of 15% with the GoI and 19% with the LIC.

The decision of the CCEA was implemented through a two-stage, competitive bidding process supported by a multi-layered, collective decision-making mechanism consisting of the Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG), the Core Group of Secretaries on Disinvestment (CGD) and the Alternative Mechanism (AM) consisting of an empowered Group of Cabinet Ministers.

The Preliminary Information Memorandum (PIM) inviting Expression of Interest (EoI) from all interested parties was issued on 07.10.2022. Only the parties found ‘Fit and Proper’ by the RBI and granted security clearance by the MHA could participate in the bidding stage, for which a Request for Proposal was issued for inviting technical and financial bids from the Qualified Interested Parties (QIPs). Of the five parties who initially submitted their expression of interest, four parties qualified as per the eligibility criteria and disqualification conditions prescribed therein, of which, two finally submitted their techno-financial bids and became Qualified Bidders (QBs) for this Transaction.

After comprehensive evaluation by the CGD and after considering the recommendations of the Alternative Mechanism, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) in its meeting held on 14/10/2026 approved M/s 10955230 Canada Inc. (parent entity M/s Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd.) as the Strategic Buyer for this Transaction for a purchase consideration of Rs.52,878.0806181 Crores (in words Rupees Fifty-Two Thousand Eight Hundred Seventy-Eight Crore Eight Lakh Six Thousand and One Hundred Eighty-One only) for the acquisition of 60.72% stake in the IDBI Bank Ltd, comprising 30.48% equity shareholding held by the Gol and 30.24% equity shareholding held by the LIC.

In such transactions, there is no a-priori benchmark for bidding. The bidders do their own valuation and submit their bids in sealed envelopes in a confidential manner. Independent agencies are hired to do a fair valuation of the enterprise contemporaneously, which is then used as a comparator to assess the reasonableness of the bids submitted.

Under this transaction, the initial bids were invited in the financial year 2025-26. For comparison, a reserve price of Rs.94.42 per share was fixed at that time, which was directly and indirectly influenced by the impacted market price. The unimpacted counter-factual was not visible at that time, except that the unimpacted pre-EoI price of the IDBI stock was Rs.42.40 per share on the last trading day before the issue of the PIM/EoI on 07.10.2022. In contrast, the impacted price was Rs.108.12 per share on the last trading day before the invitation of initial bids on 08.01.2026. The initial bids fell short of the reserve price arrived at that time and were not approved. When it became known that the initial bids have not succeeded, the impacted stock market price itself corrected, and fell significantly below the discovered bid price of Rs.75 per share.

Subsequently, in exercise of the powers delegated and conferred upon the collective decision-making mechanism, and to enhance the value of the transaction as far as possible, sealed bids reflecting their best offers were invited from the qualified bidders in the financial year 2026-27. The stock price of the IDBI Stock was Rs.70.38 per share on the trading day last before the invitation of best offer bids on 18.05.2026.

The stock market price of the narrowly traded IDBI stock continued to be volatile and fluctuated both above and below the bid discovered price with a high-low range of Rs.118.38 to Rs.61.01 per share over the valuation period. The stock market price was consequently disregarded, as it tended to misalign valuation with the intrinsic value of the enterprise. Instead, Relative Valuation by the Market Multiple Method, which overcomes this problem, was used to determine the fair market value of the enterprise on the basis of 31st March, 2026 closing accounts of all public sector banks. Additionally, the Asset Valuation Method, which considers both tangible and intangible assets, including land and properties along with the liabilities, was used to determine the fair net asset value of the enterprise as per the 31st March, 2026 audited accounts of the IDBI Bank Ltd.

Accordingly, the fair valuation of the enterprise was carried out by two professional valuation agencies using two independent methodologies as explained above. The average of these fair valuations was Rs.75.99 per share, which served as the benchmark price for the evaluation of the qualified bids. Since the winning best offer bid of Rs.81 per share was above the benchmark price, as well as fair value estimates of both the independent valuation agencies, it was adjudged to be reasonable and approved.   

The successful bidder will be required to present its credentials to the Reserve Bank of India in accordance with the Fit and Proper Assessment conducted at the EoI stage and submit its roadmap for the compliance of regulatory conditions prescribed therein. Once completed, this will be the largest FDI in the financial sector of our economy so far.

The CCEA has also delegated powers to the Alternative Mechanism to undertake minority stake sales of the GoI residual shareholding (15% of the total shareholding of the IDBI Bank Ltd.) through the open market in accordance with the standard operating procedure. The LIC will be free to manage its residual shareholding in accordance with its internal procedures while ensuring compliance with the directions of its regulators.

Read FAQs at: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2323320&v=7®=48&lang=2

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Quality Infrastructure, Clean Energy and Consumer Safety Take Centre Stage at the National Celebration of World Standards Day 2026
Union Cabinet Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi Highlights Role of Standards in India’s Clean Energy Transition
MoS Shri B. L. Verma and Smt. Nimuben J Bambhaniya Address BIS World Standards Day Event in Delhi
BIS Launches Silver Refinery Scheme and Roadmap for Sustainable Agriculture and Sustainable Manufacturing 
New Indian Standards Released for the Emerging Technology, Clean Energy, Traditional Medicine & Healthcare
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi

In a major push toward strengthening national quality infrastructure and accelerating India’s clean energy transition, Bureau of Indian Standards unveiled BIS Silver Refinery Scheme, New Indian Standards on emerging technologies & clean energy mobility and a standardization roadmap for sustainable agriculture and manufacturing on the occasion of World Standards Day 2026 at the national event hosted in New Delhi. 

Delivering the presidential address to standardization professionals, academicians, industry representatives and senior officials; Shri Pralhad Joshi, Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, and New & Renewable Energy, and Education; emphasized India’s commitment to quality: “Under the vision of PM Narendra Modi ji, our journey towards Viksit Bharat is driven by a single mantra: Quality, Quality, and only Quality.” Speaking on this year’s theme, ‘Shared Vision for a Better World: SDG 7 (Clean & Affordable Energy)’, Shri Joshi highlighted the role of Indian Standards developed by BIS in shaping India’s energy transformation.

Congratulating BIS on its ongoing efforts to expand the quality ecosystem in the country, Shri B. L. Verma, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution and Social Justice & Empowerment, underscored the fundamental impact of standards in improving quality of life of every citizen.  Smt. Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, emphasized the consumer-centric aspect of standardization. She underscored the need to expand standard development into newer domains, ensuring a balanced ecosystem that simultaneously drives industrial growth and protects consumer welfare.

Commending the landmark achievements of BIS in the recent years, Smt. Nidhi Khare, IAS, Secretary, Department of Consumer Affairs, underscored the pivotal role of standardization in establishing uniformity, consistency, and process institutionalization across public procurement and regulation. She stressed that effective consumer protection must be preventive driven by robust testing, digital enforcement, and conformity assessments.

Welcoming the delegates, Director General of BIS, Shri Sanjay Garg, said, "Standards are vital enablers of innovation, technology development, and industrial strength." He announced that BIS is among the world's first national standardization bodies to make standards’ development and its access completely digital for all stakeholders. He also highlighted major reforms at BIS supporting Ease of Doing Business.

Launch of BIS Silver Refinery Scheme

The BIS certification scheme for silver refineries and mints, extends structured purity assurance and hallmarking to silver bullion and coins across India and establishes a national framework for silver purity modelled after the existing Gold Refinery Scheme. 

Following the gazette notification of Amendment No. 1 to Indian Standard IS 2112:2025 (Silver and Silver Alloys, Jewellery/Artefacts — Fineness and Marking), fine silver bullion and coins of three purity grades: 999.9, 999.5, and 999.0 parts per thousand (ppt), have been included in scope of the standard, with provision for hallmarking by BIS licensed refineries and mints.

Under the scheme, BIS will grant license to qualified silver refineries and mints after assessing their technical competence, refining processes, and testing infrastructure. Licensed facilities will be authorized to apply the official BIS hallmark to silver bullion and coins conforming to the prescribed requirements.

For assured authenticity and traceability across the precious metals supply chain, hallmarked silver bullion and coins will bear a standardized BIS mark comprising of the BIS Standard Mark accompanied by the word SILVER, purity grade (999.9, 999.5, or 999.0), the manufacturer’s identification mark and a unique serial number for batch traceability. 

The standard prescribes rigorous sampling and testing protocols for refineries and mints to determine the silver content in bullion and coins. These include advance analytical methods such as Gravimetric testing (IS 2113), ICP-OES difference method (IS 16900 / ISO 15096) and Spark-OES difference methods (IS 19563 / ISO 18214).

 https://youtu.be/SrF8K82bTow

Launch of BIS Digital Standard Reader – BIS Digital Standard Reader is a web-based platform that converts XML-formatted Indian Standards into interactive SMART standards. Designed to enhance accessibility, the tool enables users to search technical content, navigate hyperlinked cross-references, access an in-built dictionary, and translate text into Indian languages. Accessible across mobile devices, tablets, and desktops, the platform also features an analytics dashboard to track usage trends and establishes an AI-ready repository for future digital services. This will make Indian Standards much user friendly and easy for adaption. 

Release of New Indian Standards - On this occasion BIS announced the rollout of 7 new Indian Standards across diverse sectors, including textiles, clean mobility, therapeutic healthcare, robotics, and building materials.

Emerging Technologies & Clean Energy Mobility -

  1. Cables for Electric Vehicle Charging Systems (IS 19967:2026): Defines construction, insulation, thermal management, and testing protocols for flexible charging cables (up to 1,100 V AC / 1,500 V DC) operating under demanding outdoor conditions across AC Modes 1–3 and DC Mode 4 systems
  2. Pedal Assisted Bicycles / EPACs (IS 19891:2026): Provides standards for design, electrical circuit safety, short-circuit/overheat protection, and anti-tampering rules for Electrically Power Assisted Cycles with continuous rated power up to 0.25 kW and speed cut-off at 25 km/h
  3. Wearable Service Robots – Lower Limb (IS 17192 Part-6:2026): Adopts international testing criteria (identical to ISO FDIS 18646-6:2025) using anthropomorphic test dummies to evaluate the motion, stability, and performance of lower-limb assistive and rehabilitation robotics.

Healthcare–

  1. Paediatric Panchakarma Droni (IS 19960:2026): assuring safety, structural stability, non-toxic coatings, and oil-resistance specifications for Paediatric Panchakarma treatment tables (Droni) for Infant (birth to 2 years) and Child (2 to 10 years)
  2. Therapeutic Footwear Specification (IS 19956:2026): Assuring clinical and mechanical safety criteria for footwear designed for diabetic and neuropathic patients. It covers pressure relief, internal depth, rocker geometry, moisture management, and antifungal properties to mitigate foot ulceration risks.

Industrial Materials & Building Products

  1. Flexible Plywood Specification (IS 19952:2026): Provides standard classifications, glue bond strength grades (moisture-resistant, BWR, and BWP), and formaldehyde emission limits for curved wood-based panels used in interior design and architecture
  2. PVC Coated Fibreglass Insect Screen (IS 19825:2026): Outlines requirements for mesh strength, UV degradation resistance, flame propagation resistance, and structural durability for fibreglass insect screening utilized in residential and commercial spaces.

Release of National Roadmaps for Standardization in the field of Sustainable Agriculture & Manufacturing

On this occasion, a strategic roadmap developed by Environment and Ecology Division Council of BIS to establish Indian Standards for the sustainable agricultural sector was released. The document addresses challenges including climate change, resource depletion, land degradation, post-harvest losses, and inefficient nutrient use. It spans 15 categories, covering soil management, water use, agricultural inputs, emerging technologies, climate services, and socio-economic support. Aligned with the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), the roadmap outlines standard formulation across three timelines: short-term (1 year), mid-term (2–3 years), and long-term (4–5 years).

In another roadmap released today, for Sustainable Manufacturing, low-carbon technologies, resource efficiency, circular economy practices, sustainable product design, digitalisation, sustainability reporting and supply-chain management have been identified as key areas for standardisation.

Award of Best Technical Committees for Development of Standards

On the Occasion of World Standards Day, BIS presents the Best Technical Committee Award to recognise the outstanding contributions, technical expertise, and collaborative efforts of experts in advancing the development of Indian Standards in the respective sectors. This year 16 distinguished technical committees have been conferred with this prestigious award. 

Addition of 6 New Academic Institutions into Standardization Framework - 

In the presence of Union Minister of State Shri B L Verma and Smt Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, BIS onboarded IIT Ropar, NIT Manipur, NIT Meghalaya, Assam Textiles Institute, and IIT Dharwad, and RGIPT (Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology) as MoU partner institution with an objective to integrate Indian standards into academic curricula and transform students into standards-ready professionals. As on date BIS has 98 number of MoU partner institutions working for integration of standards in academic curricula, collaborative R&D projects for standardization as well as offering internship in BIS and industry exposure to the students.

Handbook on Good Practices for Safety in the Laboratory

BIS has published a comprehensive booklet, ‘Good Practices for Safety in Laboratory,’ drawing on key standards (including IS 4209, IS 4906, and IS 9457). The reference handbook covers hazard identification, protective equipment, contamination control, and safe waste disposal for chemical, radiochemical, and microbiological facilities.

Release of Educational Comic books –

On this occasion, two new comic books on Indian Standards for Toys and Hallmarking were released by BIS to foster awareness among children about the importance of standards, quality and consumer protection from an early age. With the addition of these titles, BIS has expanded its collection to 13 comic books, strengthening its efforts to promote consumer awareness through print and digital platforms.

On the occasion of World Standards Day 2026, global standardization bodies ISO, IEC and ITU jointly released a video message sharing how shared standards build system-trust, accelerate innovation, and support sustainable trade. As India’s national standardization body, BIS participates in over 600 technical committees across ISO and IEC to align international standard development with India’s strategic interests.

Source: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC) Celebrates World Standards Day 2026 at TEC New Delhi, Highlighting India's Pivotal Role in Global Telecommunication Standardization
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC), the National Standardization Body in the telecommunications sector under the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, celebrated World Standards Day 2026 today at Manak Hall, TEC, New Delhi reaffirming India's commitment to strengthening its role in global technology development and standardization.

The momentous event was attended by all senior officers of TEC. The celebration highlighted TEC's instrumental role in formulating telecommunications standards, driving domestic technological self-reliance, and actively contributing to international standardization bodies such as the International Telecommunication Union's Standardization Sector (ITU-T).

Milestone Achieved in Standardization

Under the Telecommunications (Framework to Notify Standards, Conformity Assessment and Certification) Rules, 2025, TEC formulates standards, recognizes Conformity Assessment Bodies (CAB) and issues certificates. TEC has released 596 standards in different technology domains including Essential requirements, Generic Requirements, Test Guides and Standard Documents of TEC. TEC has designated 82 CABs till date and further more than 5400 certificates have been issued.

TEC’s Leadership and Contribution to Global Standardization

Functioning under the Ministry of Communications, TEC serves as the national body for developing standards for telecommunication equipment, services, and networks in India. During the event, the Senior DDG & Head of TEC, Shri Syed Tausif Abbas commended the relentless efforts of TEC officers for representing India globally by holding pivotal leadership roles across various ITU-T Study Groups.

The address further highlighted that robust national standards formulated by TEC not only safeguard consumer interests and ensure network security, interoperability, and quality of service (QoS), but also successfully align India's digital ecosystem with global benchmarks.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Government Constitutes Committee to Examine Issues Relating to Sugarcane Farmers and the Sugar Sector
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has constituted a committee under the chairmanship of Prof. Ramesh Chand, former Member of NITI Aayog, to examine issues raised by sugarcane farmers and recommend appropriate measures for addressing their concerns.

The constitution of the Committee follows the decisions taken during a meeting of representatives of sugarcane farmers from Karnataka and Maharashtra with the Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and the Union Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.

The Committee will examine the demand for an increase in remunerative returns to sugarcane farmers, taking into account cultivation costs and other relevant factors. It will also examine the demand for revision of the ex-mill Minimum Selling Price (MSP) of sugar in the context of sugar production costs, market realisations, and the financial viability of sugar mills.

Other key areas of examination will include existing mechanisms for testing and reporting sugar recovery, measures to ensure transparent verification of recovery, and prevailing sugarcane weighment practices at sugar mills, including the adequacy of calibration, inspection and verification mechanisms.

The Committee will also examine prevailing practices, relating to deductions from the weight of mechanically harvested sugarcane and assess the extent of actual losses, if any, arising from mechanised harvesting. It will evaluate the financial impact of the present practices on the cane price payable to farmers and may consider any other related matters deemed necessary.

The Committee will consult all stakeholders, including farmers’ representatives, sugar mill associations, State Governments and other experts or organisations, as considered necessary. The Committee will submit its report, containing its findings and specific recommendations, as early as possible, for consideration by the competent authority.

The Chairman of the committee, Prof. Ramesh Chand, an eminent agricultural economist and public policy expert, served as a Member of NITI Aayog from 2015 to 2026 and previously as Director of ICAR-NIAP and Member of the Fifteenth Finance Commission. He has extensive expertise in agricultural development, farmers’ issues, food security, agricultural markets and pricing policy.

The Committee comprises the Agriculture Commissioner, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; Joint Secretary (Sugar), Department of Food and Public Distribution and Joint Secretary (Legal Metrology), Department of Consumer Affairs as members.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Communications

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to honor top-performing States/UTs, District Police and Police Stations for recovery of lost mobile handsets through Sanchar Saathi
Awards to be presented in upcoming National, Zonal & State level Events of DoT
Number of handsets traceable and recovered are to be key performance parameters
Posted On: 14 OCT 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India will recognize and award the best-performing States/Union Territories (UTs), Police Districts and Police Stations for their exemplary efforts in recovering lost/stolen mobile handsets traced through the Sanchar Saathi portal - a citizen centric initiative of DoT to empower mobile subscribers, strengthen their security and increase awareness about citizen centric initiatives of the Government. The awards will be presented during the upcoming National, Zonal & State level Events of DoT.

The initiative aims to acknowledge the significant contribution of State/UT Police authorities in tracing and recovering lost or stolen mobile handsets and returning them to their rightful owners. It also seeks to encourage greater coordination between DoT, its License Service Area (LSA) field units, police authorities and telecom operators, promote the adoption of effective recovery practices, and improve recovery outcomes for citizens across the country.

The awards will be based on measurable performance parameters, i.e based on accuracy (i.e handsets recovered against trace generated) and total number of handsets recovered etc. These parameters will help recognize the scale, accuracy and timeliness of recovery efforts undertaken by States/UTs, Police Districts and Police Stations. The detailed evaluation methodology and applicable assessment period will be finalized by DoT.

The State/UT-wise data on mobile handsets traced and recovered through the Sanchar Saathi portal is publicly available on the portal’s dashboard, which also provides visibility into recovery trends. This data will serve as an important reference for assessing performance and identifying high-performing jurisdictions and police units.

Sanchar Saathi portal facilitates the blocking and tracing of lost or stolen mobile handsets through the Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR) facility. When a reported handset is subsequently detected on a telecom network, traceability information is generated and made available to the respective Police authorities, supporting police efforts to locate and recover the device. An alert regarding the traceability is also sent to the citizen through SMS and email.

The initiative reflects the importance of close coordination among DoT, its LSA field units, Telecom Service Providers and State/UT Police authorities in strengthening mobile security and protecting citizens’ digital assets. The proposed awards will provide a platform to recognize outstanding work, encourage healthy performance-driven competition and promote the sharing of successful practices across jurisdictions.

DoT reiterates its commitment to strengthening the Sanchar Saathi ecosystem and supporting law-enforcement agencies in improving the recovery of lost and stolen mobile handsets. Citizens can access the portal at www.sancharsaathi.gov.in or use Sanchar Saathi Mobile app to report lost or stolen mobile handsets and avail following citizen centric services.

Services at the fingertips of every citizen

Sanchar Saathi brings the following citizen-centric services on a single platform:

Chakshu – Report suspected fraud communication and spam: Report suspicious calls, SMS or WhatsApp messages – such as fake KYC or bill- payment alerts, impersonation of Government, police or bank officials, and fraudulent investment, job or loan offers – in a few simple steps.

Know mobile connections in your name: Check all mobile connections issued on your identity and report those which you have not taken or no longer require, so that they cannot be misused.

Block your lost or stolen mobile handset: Block the handset across the networks of all telecom operators so that it cannot be used anywhere in India, enable its tracing, and unblock it once it is found.

Know the genuineness of your mobile handset: Verify a handset through its IMEI number before buying a new or second-hand phone.

Report incoming international calls with Indian numbers: Report calls from abroad that are disguised as domestic (+91) numbers, helping the Government act against illegal telecom set-ups.

Trusted Contact Details: Verify the genuine customer care numbers, email IDs and website links of banks and financial institutions before sharing any information.

Keep Yourself Aware: Access awareness material on prevailing fraud trends such as fake loan apps, investment scams, fake job calls and fake traffic challans

DoT is fully committed to ensure safety of citizens through its proactive actions for curbing misuse of telecom resources for cybercrime and financial frauds. Sanchar Saathi is also available as mobile app and can be downloaded from:

  • For Android:: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.dot.app.sancharsaathi
  • For iOS: https://apps.apple.com/app/sanchar-saathi/id6739700695
