item.title: From Regional Identity to Shared National Heritage
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Culture
item.description: Ministry of Culture From Regional Identity to Shared National Heritage PM Mementos brings local traditions and cultural expressions of Madhya Pradesh into a wider national space Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi The 22 mementos from Madhya Pradesh featured in the 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction offer more than a collection of artworks, photographs and commemorative objects. Taken together, they form a visual map of the State’s living heritage, connecting traditions and historic places with indigenous artistic expression, ecological heritage, public…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
From Regional Identity to Shared National Heritage
PM Mementos brings local traditions and cultural expressions of Madhya Pradesh into a wider national space
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

The 22 mementos from Madhya Pradesh featured in the 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction offer more than a collection of artworks, photographs and commemorative objects. Taken together, they form a visual map of the State’s living heritage, connecting traditions and historic places with indigenous artistic expression, ecological heritage, public institutions and symbols of India’s national identity.

The 22 mementos from Madhya Pradesh illustrate a central idea behind PM Mementos: a gift may originate in a particular place, community or tradition, but its story can become part of a larger national cultural memory.

A State told through its places, people and traditions

The collection moves across the cultural landscape of Madhya Pradesh. From Ujjain and Khajuraho to Udayagiri, Maheshwar, Shajapur, Neemuch, Khandwa and the forests of Sanjay Tiger Reserve, the collection reflects the many layers of the State’s identity.

 

Among the notable mementos is a small-scale metal model of Kandariya Mahadev Temple, Khajuraho, which brings the architectural and sculptural legacy of one of Madhya Pradesh’s most celebrated heritage sites into a contemporary form. Another memento represents Vishnu as Varaha from the Udayagiri Caves, linking the present with the State’s ancient sculptural heritage.

The collection also carries the memory of individuals who contributed to India’s intellectual and social development. A statue of Dr. Hari Singh Gour, educationist, jurist and social reformer, represents the contribution of education and institution-building to the State’s public life.

A framed photograph of Maheshwar Fort and its ghats highlights the architecture of the State.

Heritage that continues to live

The collection also demonstrates that heritage is not confined to monuments inherited from the past. It continues to be expressed through the beliefs, artistic practices and landscapes of contemporary communities.

The Gond Tree of Life paintings are an important example. Rooted in the traditional Gond artistic vocabulary, the works bring indigenous visual expression into the national collection, demonstrating how community-based artistic traditions continue to find contemporary forms of expression.

The collection’s numerous representations of Mahakaleshwar in Ujjain, alongside depictions of Maa Rajarajeshwari of Shajapur, Mahamaya Bhadwa Mataji of Neemuch and Shri Dadaji Dhuniwale Mandir of Khandwa, similarly point to the continuing role of sacred traditions in the cultural life of the State.

From regional identity to a shared national story

The collection also moves beyond regional identity towards symbols of a wider Indian imagination.

A wooden representation of the Lion Capital of Ashoka, incorporating the Ashoka Chakra and other elements of the national emblem, connects Madhya Pradesh’s local expressions of craftsmanship with one of India’s most recognisable symbols of national identity. An Atmanirbhar Bharat Jan Sampark Maha Abhiyan commemorative poster, meanwhile, represents a more contemporary aspect of public life.

The PM Mementos initiative gives this journey a public dimension. A memento presented during a moment of public interaction begins as a personal expression of appreciation or local identity. Through the e-auction, it enters a wider public space, where citizens can engage with the object and the story it carries. Each object retains its local character while collectively contributing to a larger story of India’s shared cultural inheritance.

Since its inception, the PM Mementos e-Auction has made thousands of gifts presented to the Prime Minister available to the public, with proceeds dedicated to the Namami Gange Programme.

The auction is currently live and has been extended until 31 October 2026. Interested bidders can place their bids online through the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal: https://pmmementos.gov.in

 

***

M Annadurai

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
item.description: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways NHAI Releases Document on ‘Wildlife Mitigation Measures & Structures’ Highlighting Strengthened Wildlife Conservation Measures Along National Highways Over Rs.19,700 crore invested in wildlife mitigation infrastructure and environmental safeguards in last five years More than 2,150 wildlife mitigation structures have been constructed and/or proposed along National Highways across the country Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi Highlighting initiatives towards integrating wildlife conservation into National Highway planning,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Releases Document on ‘Wildlife Mitigation Measures & Structures’ Highlighting Strengthened Wildlife Conservation Measures Along National Highways
Over Rs.19,700 crore invested in wildlife mitigation infrastructure and environmental safeguards in last five years
More than 2,150 wildlife mitigation structures have been constructed and/or proposed along National Highways across the country
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

Highlighting initiatives towards integrating wildlife conservation into National Highway planning, design, and implementation, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) released a document on ‘Wildlife Mitigation Measures & Structures’ Commemorating ‘National Wildlife Week’ from 2nd - 8th October 2026.  The document was recently released by Shri Nitin Gadkari, Hon’ble Minister for Road Transport and Highways during Chintan Shivir held in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat.  The document reflects NHAI’s approach towards developing National Highway infrastructure that balances requirements of connectivity and mobility with environmental sustainability and wildlife conservation.

Over last five years, around Rs. 19,700 crores have been invested in wildlife mitigation infrastructure and related environmental protection measures across National Highway projects. These interventions are aimed at addressing key challenges associated with National Highway infrastructure development, including habitat fragmentation, barrier effects and wildlife–vehicle collisions, while maintaining safe movement of traffic.

NHAI’s mitigation planning is guided by the ecological sensitivity of project corridors, wildlife movement patterns and the technical feasibility of infrastructure design. This enables wildlife mitigation measures to be planned according to the specific ecological and engineering requirements of individual highway corridors.

More than 2,150 Wildlife Mitigation Structures

The document outlines a structured framework for wildlife mitigation planning incorporating both structural measures including underpasses, overpasses, culverts and canopy crossings as well as non-structural interventions like signage, fencing and speed regulation etc. More than 2,150 wildlife mitigation structures have been constructed and/or proposed along National Highways across the country. These also include Animal Under Passes (AUPs), bridge-integrated crossings such as major bridge-cum-AUPs and minor bridge-cum-AUPs, culverts adapted for faunal movement, canopy crossings and other specialised structures.

As part of the structural mitigation measures, around Rs. 4,600 crores have been invested in animal underpasses, Rs. 650 crores in animal overpasses, Rs. 8,300 crores in viaducts, Rs. 2,800 crores in tunnels, Rs. 2,500 crores in major bridges and Rs. 500 crores in minor bridges. These structures facilitate safe wildlife movement across highway corridors and help maintain ecological connectivity between habitats.

NHAI has complemented these structural measures with a range of non-structural interventions aimed at minimising disturbance and improving habitat conditions such as noise barriers, reptile crossings, rainwater harvesting and other wildlife management interventions.

Integrated Approach to Wildlife Protection

To guide wildlife towards designated crossing structures and reduce the possibility of animal–vehicle conflicts, guide fencing and noise barriers have been provided at over 300 km of National Highway alignments.

NHAI has also established monitoring mechanisms, including camera trapping, to assess wildlife movement patterns and support periodic evaluation of mitigation measures. Wildlife–vehicle collision hotspots are identified and appropriate measures, including speed-regulation boards and signages, are provided to minimise risks to wildlife as well as highway users.

Balancing Infrastructure Development with Ecological Conservation

Document also underscores the importance of collaboration between the conservation community and agencies involved in National Highway infrastructure development. The approach adopted by NHAI seeks to ensure that mitigation measures are incorporated at different stages of National Highway development, enabling infrastructure expansion to be undertaken with due regard to biodiversity conservation and statutory environmental compliance requirements. The detailed document is available on NHAI website at https://nhai.gov.in/nhai/sites/default/files/mix_file/NHAI-Wildlife_Mitigation_Measures_and_Structures.pdf  

Covering recent initiatives and project implementations, the document reflects NHAI's commitment to incorporate various environmental protection measures for National Highway infrastructure development. It will serve as a reference framework, documenting the range of mitigation measures and structures being adopted across National Highway projects.

***

GDH/DS

item.title: Union Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw Launches World Bank Group’s ‘World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence’ in New Delhi
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Electronics & IT
item.description: Ministry of Electronics & IT Union Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw Launches World Bank Group’s ‘World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence’ in New Delhi Report sets out a framework for developing economies to harness AI for development through adoption, adaptation and advancement IndiaAI Mission, MeitY and the World Bank Group jointly host the India launch; policymakers, development experts and technology leaders deliberate on scaling AI for inclusive development High-level panel and State AI Showcase examine how India can move from isolated AI pilots to…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Union Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw Launches World Bank Group’s ‘World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence’ in New Delhi
Report sets out a framework for developing economies to harness AI for development through adoption, adaptation and advancement
IndiaAI Mission, MeitY and the World Bank Group jointly host the India launch; policymakers, development experts and technology leaders deliberate on scaling AI for inclusive development
High-level panel and State AI Showcase examine how India can move from isolated AI pilots to evidence-based scale-up across sectors
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, the Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Railways, and Information and Broadcasting, today launched the World Bank Group’s World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence at an event held at The Oberoi, New Delhi. The Report examines the opportunities and challenges that Artificial Intelligence (AI) presents for developing economies, and sets out a framework for countries to harness AI for development through adoption, adaptation and advancement.

The launch was organised by the IndiaAI Mission, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, in collaboration with the World Bank Group. It brought together senior policymakers, global development experts, technology leaders and practitioners to deliberate on how India can maximise, and safely sustain, the development gains from AI. The programme also featured a State AI Showcase, in which States and innovators presented AI-enabled solutions from across the country.

The Report notes that AI can widen access to expertise, raise productivity and improve the delivery of services in developing economies. AI-enabled tools are already being deployed in medical screening, agricultural decision-making and education, extending scarce expertise to larger sections of the population. The Report further emphasises that these gains rest on strong foundations, including reliable electricity and connectivity, computing infrastructure, quality data, skills, education systems and capable institutions.

Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Minister of Electronics and IT delivered the keynote address and formally presented the Report. The Union Minister underlined India’s approach of democratising technology, so that the benefits of Artificial Intelligence reach citizens, enterprises and institutions across the country.

“AI is changing the lives of ordinary people. In Baramati, sugarcane yields rose by 40 per cent with 30 per cent less water and fertiliser, for farmers who have never used a computer  simply through voice on a phone. In healthcare, TB detection has increased by 35 per cent. Examples like these can change lives across the Global South and the world,” said Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw.

The Union Minister added that the Baramati initiative draws on satellite, IoT and weather data and has also lowered labour costs. In Gujarat, AgriStack is being used by 5 lakh farmers, and AI for animal health through Sarlaben is benefiting 3 crore cattle and their farmers.

India has emerged as a significant ecosystem for the development and deployment of AI, with applications in healthcare, agriculture, education, governance, financial services and other sectors of public and economic importance. Through the IndiaAI Mission, the Government of India is building a comprehensive AI ecosystem across seven pillars: IndiaAI Compute Capacity, IndiaAI Innovation Centre for indigenous foundation models, IndiaAI Datasets Platform (AIKosh), IndiaAI Application Development Initiative, IndiaAI FutureSkills, IndiaAI Startup Financing, and Safe & Trusted AI.

The Mission seeks to strengthen India’s capabilities across the AI value chain, while ensuring that AI development remains inclusive, responsible and suited to India’s scale, diversity and multilingual context. The Government’s approach focuses on democratising access to compute, data and models, addressing India-specific challenges, and creating economic and employment opportunities. Under the Safe & Trusted AI pillar, the Government is supporting the development of indigenous tools and frameworks for responsible AI, including AI bias mitigation, algorithm auditing, explainable AI, privacy-preserving AI and deepfake detection, and has put in place institutional mechanisms for AI governance and safety.

The India launch provided a platform for policymakers and practitioners to examine how successful AI pilots can be identified, evaluated and scaled to deliver measurable development outcomes, and how the risks from AI can be safeguarded against.

The event commenced with welcome remarks by Shri Sudeep Srivastava, Chief Operating Officer, IndiaAI Mission and Joint Secretary, MeitY, and Dr. Somik Lall, Director of Strategy, Development Economics, World Bank Group.

“One of the key messages of the World Development Report is not about creating artificial intelligence but deploying it. India has a unique opportunity to bring together institutions, markets and AI to transform millions of lives,” said Dr. Somik Lall.

Delivering the keynote lecture on “From AI Pilots to Scale: The Promise of AI in India”, Dr. Michael Kremer, Chief Economist and Senior Vice President, World Bank Group, highlighted that India’s progress in AI holds lessons for the wider developing world. “India’s huge strides in AI is not just addressing its own problems but broader development challenges for the world,” he said.

Illustrating examples from weather advisory for farmers and EdTech solutions in Andhra Pradesh, he said, “For the scale up of AI solutions, we need a full stack approach - not just elements of the software but humans and institutional elements that come along with it.”

Dr. Kremer cited India’s AI-based monsoon forecasting as an example for the world. The Government of India, through its meteorological agencies and the Ministry of Agriculture, tested and combined multiple AI models, including open-access models, and delivered the forecasts to millions of farmers through text, voice and AI-powered advisories. The model predicted the unusual 2025 monsoon, and Ethiopia is now following India’s lead. He said the case shows that where commercial incentives are weak but the social potential is high, government has an important role to play.

This was followed by a presentation of the key findings of the Report by Dr. Gaurav Nayyar, Director, World Development Report 2026.

“India is already approaching the path of AI for development by adapting tools to local contexts with the government playing the role of an enabler, user and regulator of this new technology. AI can solve for developing countries like India in decades, what could not have been done in a century,” said Dr. Nayyar.

The presentation set out the Report’s core messages for developing countries: be optimistic, be strategic and be pragmatic. Countries should adopt and adapt AI, then advance; focus on adapting AI tools to local contexts rather than spending billions of dollars building advanced systems from scratch; and make cost-conscious choices as enablers, users and regulators of AI. It also noted that the risk of job disruption is less imminent in developing countries, and that the countries with the most to gain from AI may be the least prepared, with only one of the world’s 25 low-income countries having published a national AI strategy.

Special remarks were delivered by Shri Neelkanth Mishra, Executive Director, World Bank Group, and Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY.

“The World Development Report aligns closely with India’s AI roadmap  compute, data and models  and sets out a sensible approach to regulation: rely on existing laws and voluntary compliance, and revisit regulation as the technology evolves,” said Shri S. Krishnan.

Shri Krishnan said that human capabilities matter most, and that, in line with the Prime Minister’s vision, work is under way on an AI Talent Mission. He added that, with among the highest AI skill penetration in the world, India can support the Global South, while enterprise adoption of AI at home must expand, and that government must remain nimble and flexible.

A high-level panel discussion on “Making AI Work for Development in India” followed. It addressed three questions: the challenges of AI adoption in India, how India can leverage AI and adapt it to local contexts and needs, and the policies required to contain the risks arising from AI. The discussion emphasised that realising the benefits of AI will require policies that ensure its gains are widely shared and its risks are tightly contained.

The panel comprised Shri Neelkanth Mishra, Executive Director, World Bank Group; Dr. Somik Lall, Director of Strategy, Development Economics, World Bank Group; Dr. Vivek Raghavan, Co-Founder, Sarvam AI; Dr. Neeraj Agrawal, Chief Program Officer, Wadhwani AI; Shri Maneesh Singh, Vice President, BharatGen; and Shri Shankar Maruwada, Co-Founder and CEO, EkStep Foundation. The session was moderated by Ms. Shereen Bhan, Managing Editor, CNBC-TV18. The panellists stressed the need to move beyond isolated pilots towards evidence-based scale-up, strengthen local capabilities, improve access to data and compute, put in place appropriate institutional frameworks, and keep AI solutions relevant to India’s diverse social and economic contexts.

The panel discussion was followed by the State AI Showcase, “AI Innovations from Across India”, which offered a pan-India perspective on how States are deploying scalable AI applications across sectors to address local and development challenges. Each presenter highlighted one key AI-enabled solution, its implementation journey and measurable impact. The presentations were:

  • Navachetana, an AI-enabled early screening initiative for children aged 0 to 6 years to detect developmental delays, presented by Shri M. Venugopal Reddy, Director, Women Development & Child Welfare Department, Andhra Pradesh;
  • MahaVISTAAR AI, a connected platform for personalised advisories, digital services and farmer engagement, presented by Shri Fahim Shaikh, PoCRA Project, Maharashtra;
  • EdskGrid, a GeoAI governance intelligence solution for education, presented by Ms. Richa Kulkarni, State Project Director, Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan and Director, School Education & Literacy, Meghalaya;
  • Vyuhaa-Cerviai, a cervical cancer screening solution for the point of care, presented by Shri Dhritiman Mallick, Co-Founder and CEO, Vyuhaa Med Data, a winner of the NCG Catch Grant; and

The showcase highlighted diverse approaches, emerging models and solutions with potential for adaptation across geographies.

The deliberations underscored the importance of building public trust in AI, and of ensuring that the technology develops in a manner that is safe, responsible and inclusive. The India launch of the World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence adds an important voice to the global dialogue on harnessing AI as an enabler of development, and reinforced the need for countries to build the foundational capabilities, institutions and policy frameworks required to translate advances in AI into broad-based and sustainable development outcomes.

The event concluded with closing remarks by Shri Md. Y. Safirulla K., IAS, Director, IndiaAI Mission.

***

Vinod Kumar / Dhanya Ranjan / Kanishk Sharma

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Department of Defence Production continues Special Campaign 6.0 with Focus on Swachhata and Reducing Pendency
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi

Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence has kick-started the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6.0 from October 2 which will continue till October 31, 2026, with a focus on Swachhata and reducing pendency across its offices. This year, the Nation-wide Campaign will also place special emphasis on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste.

As part of Special Campaign 6.0, the Department has laid particular emphasis on field and outstation offices providing public services, in addition to attached and subordinate offices, Autonomous Bodies and Public Sector Undertakings.

During the preparatory phase of the campaign which lasted between 15th and 30th September 2026, the department conducted various activities including mobilising offices, officers and ground functionaries; identifying pending references and cleanliness campaign sites; assessing redundant material for disposal; planning for efficient space management; disposal of scrap; record management; and identifying measures for effective collection and segregation of e-waste.

The Department of Defence Production had previously recorded significant outcomes during Special Campaign 5.0, with 17.42 lakhs sq. ft. of space freed and ₹15.62 cr. earned through scrap disposal. In addition to this, 27,500 physical files were weeded out and 1,890 electronic files were closed.

*****

SR/Labh

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry Of Social Justice & Empowerment To Hold Regional Review Meeting In Diu Tomorrow
Meeting To Review Implementation Of Key Welfare, Social Empowerment And Social Defence Schemes With Focus On Last-Mile Delivery, Beneficiary Saturation And Outcome-Oriented Implementation
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India, will convene a Regional Review Meeting (RRM) in the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu (DNH&DD), in Diu tomorrow to undertake a comprehensive review of the implementation of major welfare, social empowerment and social defence schemes in the Western Region of the country.

The meeting will bring together senior representatives from the States of Rajasthan, Goa and Maharashtra, along with senior officers of the Union Territory Administration of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu.

Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, will address the meeting and outline the key implementation priorities and objectives of the Regional Review Meeting.

Under the guidance of Hon'ble Administrator of UT of DNH&DD Shri Praful Patel, several senior officers are participating in the Regional Review Meeting. These include Secretary, Social Welfare Department, Shri Ashish Mohan, Collector, Diu, Shri Rahul Dev Boora and Director-cum-Deputy Secretary, Social Welfare Department Shri Puneet Kulshreshtha.

Senior representatives from the participating States including Shri Lalit Kumar, Director Department of Social Welfare, Government of Rajasthan; Shri Dipak Desai, Director Department of Social Welfare, Government of Goa; Ms Deepa Mudhol Mundhe, Commissioner, Department of Social Welfare, Government of Maharashtra and Ms Sonali Mule, Director under Government of Maharashtra, will participate in the deliberations.

Senior officers from the Ministry attending the Regional Review Meeting include Additional Secretary Smt. Debolina Thakur, along with Joint Secretaries Shri Sajeesh Kumar N.,  Shri Parveen Kumar Thind, Dr. Sandeep Rewaji Rathod, Deputy Director General, Smt. Pratima Gupta and Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, Director, among other senior officers of the Ministry.

The Regional Review Meeting is aimed at strengthening institutional coordination between the Ministry, the participating States and the Union Territory Administration and ensuring effective, transparent, accountable and outcome-oriented implementation of social justice and empowerment programmes, with particular emphasis on last-mile delivery, beneficiary coverage and saturation, efficient utilisation of resources and measurable outcomes.

The meeting will provide an institutional platform for a scheme-wise assessment of progress, identification of implementation gaps and challenges, sharing of best practices and formulation of time-bound corrective and follow-up measures to improve the delivery of benefits to eligible beneficiaries.

Scheme-wise Review of Major Programmes

The Regional Review Meeting will undertake a detailed scheme-wise review of major programmes of the Department of Social Justice & Empowerment, including the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY), measures for strengthening the enforcement machinery under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, and the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR).

The review will assess physical and financial progress, beneficiary coverage and saturation, utilisation of funds, institutional mechanisms, implementation of statutory safeguards, awareness and outreach measures, rehabilitation and social reintegration initiatives, as well as convergence with the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA).

A detailed discussion and open-house session will provide an opportunity to examine implementation challenges and identify practical solutions relating to beneficiary identification and saturation, inter-departmental convergence, monitoring and data management, fund utilisation, grievance redressal and dissemination of best practices and replicable models. The session will also focus on evolving time-bound corrective measures wherever required.

Review of Scholarships, Senior Citizen Welfare and NAMASTE

The day-long deliberations will also cover key welfare and social empowerment initiatives, including Scholarship Schemes, Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) and the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE).

The review of Scholarship Schemes will focus on beneficiary coverage, application and verification processes, timely disbursement of assistance, Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)-related issues and measures to strengthen outreach among eligible students, particularly those who remain outside the existing coverage.

Under AVYAY, the review will assess initiatives relating to the welfare, protection and empowerment of senior citizens, including institutional care, active ageing, social security, accessibility, support services and convergence with programmes and interventions of the Union Territory Administration.

The review of NAMASTE will focus on the identification and profiling of sanitation workers and waste pickers, occupational safety and dignity, access to social security and health benefits, mechanisation of sanitation operations, capacity building, livelihood support and convergence with other welfare and social protection schemes.

Focus on Last-Mile Delivery and Measurable Outcomes

A dedicated Outcome Review Session will assess the extent of coverage and saturation of eligible beneficiaries, quality and timeliness of service delivery, implementation bottlenecks, awareness and outreach mechanisms, technology-enabled monitoring, grievance redressal and feedback systems, and convergence between Central Government schemes and programmes implemented by the States and Union Territory Administration.

Particular emphasis will be placed on last-mile delivery and measurable outcomes, with the objective of ensuring that government interventions translate into tangible improvements in the lives of intended beneficiaries.

The meeting will identify priority interventions and specific action points for the participating States and the Union Territory, with emphasis on strengthening implementation mechanisms, improving outreach, addressing gaps in beneficiary identification and ensuring timely and transparent delivery of benefits.

Way Forward

The concluding session will consolidate the key observations, priorities and recommendations emerging from the deliberations. The Way Forward will include finalisation of action points and responsibilities, strengthened coordination between the Ministry, States and Union Territory Administration, time-bound resolution of implementation issues, improved monitoring of physical and financial progress and submission of follow-up Action Taken Reports (ATRs) by the concerned authorities.

The Regional Review Meeting is expected to further strengthen the institutional framework for effective implementation of social justice, social empowerment and social defence programmes in the Western Region. It will also reinforce the Government's commitment to inclusive development, social protection, dignity, equal opportunity and empowerment of vulnerable and disadvantaged sections of society, with a continued focus on ensuring that the benefits of government schemes reach the last mile.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN AIR FORCE CELEBRATES 94TH  AIR FORCE DAY AT AIR FORCE STATION HINDAN
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Air Force (IAF) commemorated its 94th Anniversary on 08 October 2026 at Air Force Station Hindan, Ghaziabad. The occasion showcased IAF's operational capabilities. technological advancement, professionalism and rich heritage. The ceremonial AF Day Parade (AFDP) was reviewed by the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh. The guests included Chief of the Army Staff, Chief of the Naval Staff former Chiefs of Air Staff and other senior military Officers and civilians

The proceedings commenced with the marching-in of the President's Colours symbolising IAF's exceptional service, professional excellence, dedication and commitment to the nation. On arrival, the Chief of the Air Staff was presented with an aerial salute by three Mi-17 1V helicopters in ' Dhwaj' formation trooping the National flag and the IAF flag. The parade was commanded by Gp Capt Manish Sharma and was followed by an investiture ceremony, during which Air Warriors were awarded medals for gallantry and distinguished service. Units were also presented citations for excellence

The theme for this year's AF Day was 'Indian Air Force: Infallible, Impervious ang Precise (भारतीय वायु सेना: अचूक, अभेद्य व सटीक),' reflecting the IAF's unwavering commitment to safeguard the nation's skies with precision, resilience and operational excellence.

In his address Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, Chief of the Air Staff highlighted that “air power is the primary means of protecting the national interest”. He also stated that “The Indian Air Force remains alert, committed and ready to meet any contingency”, emphasising that operational capability and readiness are moving in the right direction. He stated that “an air force can have the most advanced aircraft in the world, but its true strength is measured by its operational preparedness—how quickly and confidently it can act whenever the call comes.” Referring to Operation Sindoor, he noted that the IAF’s swift transition into combat operations demonstrated its “destructive power as well as the effective Air Defence operations”. He further underlined that “‘Infallible, Impervious, Precise’ is not just a tagline; it is the manifestation of our strength and resolve.”

Reiterating the IAF’s commitment to technological advancement and self-reliance, he stated that “Atmanirbharta is our guiding principle”, while emphasising that emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence and autonomous systems, would be integrated while keeping human authority at the core. He also stressed that “success in modern conflict demands deep synergy” and that joint planning and integrated combat application with the Army and Navy is a daily activity. On the aspect of space, he mentioned that “ Space is a natural extension of air domain” also highlighting the growing collaboration with ISRO and domestic space industry including IAF’s role in the Gaganyaan mission.

A static display of IAF assets provided the spectators and media personnel an opportunity to view the wide spectrum of the IAF's operational and combat capabilities Fighter aircraft, helicopters, Surface-to-Air and Surface-to-Surface Guided Weapon Systems, Radars and one way attack unmanned aerial systems were showcased at the parade. The display highlighted IAF's continuing focus on 'Make in India' and indigenous capability development. Five Unit Citations were presented to 24 Squadron ‘The Hawks’, 110 Helicopter Unit ‘The Vanguards’, 200 Squadron ‘Skanda’, 2402 Squadron ‘Vajra’ and the Electronic Warfare Range.

The celebration also featured a performance by Team Shakti, the IAF's           all-women Air Warrior Drill Team. Known for its precision, agility and discipline, the team showcased synchronised movements and complex formations, reflecting professionalism and empowerment of women Air Warriors.

The IAF Drummers Team, comprising 33 young Air Warriors, presented a vibrant display featuring snare drums, roto drums, bass drums and cymbals, accompanied by dynamic formations and acrobatic movements

The event also featured a spectacular Aerial Display by IAF Heritage Flight showcasing the rich legacy of Indian Military Aviation. An aerial display by a vintage 'Tiger Moth' aircraft enthralled the audience and provided a befitting tribute to the glorious heritage of the IAF.

Following the celebrations at Air Force Station Hindan, the Air Force Day aerial display will be conducted at Namo Ghat, Varanasi, on 25 October 2026

item.title: Department of Telecommunications hosts High-Level Roundtable with State IT Ministers and Secretaries to Accelerate Digital Connectivity and Infrastructure Rollout
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Communications
item.description: Ministry of Communications Department of Telecommunications hosts High-Level Roundtable with State IT Ministers and Secretaries to Accelerate Digital Connectivity and Infrastructure Rollout Roundtable chaired by Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia along with Minister of State Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani “To realize Viksit Bharat @2047, we must act as Team India by accelerating Right of Way approvals, pushing BharatNet and 4G saturation to the last mile”: Shri Scindia to State Ministers Centre, States/UTs Reaffirm Commitment to Faster Telecom Infrastructure Deployment and Citizen-Centric…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Department of Telecommunications hosts High-Level Roundtable with State IT Ministers and Secretaries to Accelerate Digital Connectivity and Infrastructure Rollout
Roundtable chaired by Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia along with Minister of State Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani
“To realize Viksit Bharat @2047, we must act as Team India by accelerating Right of Way approvals, pushing BharatNet and 4G saturation to the last mile”: Shri Scindia to State Ministers
Centre, States/UTs Reaffirm Commitment to Faster Telecom Infrastructure Deployment and Citizen-Centric Digital Services
State Government IT Ministers and Secretaries discussed RoW Reforms, BharatNet, 4G Connectivity and Digital Inclusion at IMC 2026 Roundtable
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, organised a high-level Roundtable Conference with State Government IT Ministers and Secretaries on the sidelines of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026. The Roundtable was chaired by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, along with Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications & Rural Development, and Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications.

The Roundtable provided a platform for structured dialogue and coordination between the Centre, States and Union Territories (UTs) on key issues concerning telecommunications, digital infrastructure and citizen-centric digital services. In line with the theme of IMC 2026, “Scale Without Boundaries”, the discussions focused on scaling digital connectivity, accelerating infrastructure deployment and strengthening Centre–State cooperation to support India’s digital transformation and the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.

Addressing the meeting, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said, "Telecom may be a Union subject, but digital infrastructure is built on State soil making our States true co-owners in driving National Broadband Mission 2.0. To realize Viksit Bharat @2047, we must act as Team India by accelerating Right of Way approvals to unlock SASCI capital incentives, pushing BharatNet and 4G saturation to the last mile, securing networks through Sanchar Saathi, and scaling Samriddh Gram so that connectivity meaningfully transforms every citizen's life."

The discussions highlighted the crucial role played by States and UTs in the successful rollout of digital communication infrastructure, particularly in addressing ground-level requirements such as Right of Way (RoW), land allocation and site access.

A key focus of the Roundtable was the implementation of the Telecommunication (Right of Way) Rules, 2024, notified by DoT under the Telecommunications Act, 2023. The Rules, which came into effect from January 1, 2025, established a uniform and transparent framework for telecom infrastructure deployment, including rationalised RoW charges and time-bound processing of applications. The Rules provide timelines of 67 days for general RoW applications and 7 days for Special Projects such as BharatNet.

It was noted that 34 States/UTs had issued Government Orders or notifications directing local bodies and line departments to follow the DoT’s RoW Rules, 2024. All 36 States/UTs are live on the Central RoW Portal. The Special Assistance for Capital Investment (SASCI) Scheme 2026–27, with an earmarked allocation of ₹4,000 crore, was also highlighted as an important enabler for strengthening implementation of RoW reforms by States and their agencies, including State PSUs, corporations and Urban Local Bodies.

The Roundtable also reviewed progress under the Amended BharatNet Programme (ABP) and the 4G Saturation Project. The ABP is aimed at upgrading the existing BharatNet network, creating incremental network infrastructure for new Gram Panchayats (GPs), connecting non-GP villages on demand and providing 1.5 crore fibre internet connections. As of August 2026, 55,780 km of Optical Fibre Cable had been laid and 28,700 Gram Panchayats had been upgraded and connected under ABP.

The meeting further highlighted the Government’s efforts to extend mobile connectivity to remote and uncovered areas through projects funded by the Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN). These initiatives were aimed at bridging the digital divide and providing 4G connectivity to villages where telecom service providers had not expanded networks due to commercial considerations. As of August 31, 2026, 25,367 mobile towers had been commissioned, covering 35,771 villages/locations across the country. The indigenous 4G stack has been used in the 4G Saturation Project implemented by BSNL.

The Roundtable also discussed the Sanchar Saathi initiative and the importance of strengthening coordination between DoT, State/UT Governments, Law Enforcement Agencies, Telecom Service Providers and other stakeholders to combat cybercrime and financial fraud. Sanchar Saathi enables citizens to report suspected fraudulent communications, check mobile connections issued in their name, report unauthorised connections, and block, report and trace lost or stolen mobile devices. The Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP) was also highlighted as an important mechanism for intelligence sharing and coordinated action against cyber fraud.

Another key initiative discussed was the Samriddh Gram Phygital Services Initiative, an integrated service delivery model aimed at translating reliable broadband connectivity into meaningful, citizen-centric services and opportunities in rural communities. Through Samriddhi Kendras, the initiative brings together services such as tele-consultations and diagnostics, digital classrooms and skilling, e-governance, banking, soil testing, drone-based agricultural services, employment opportunities and e-commerce under one roof. The model was being piloted in Umri in Madhya Pradesh, Chaurawala in Uttar Pradesh and Narakoduru in Andhra Pradesh and has been recognised globally as the winner of the WSIS Prizes 2026 under Action Line C6 – Enabling Environment.

The Roundtable concluded with a shared commitment among the Centre, States/UTs and the telecom industry to strengthen coordination, accelerate digital infrastructure deployment, facilitate adoption of emerging technologies and expand citizen-centric digital services. The discussions reaffirmed the collective resolve to build a digitally empowered and connected India and advance the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.

Team India, building a connected Bharat. 🇮🇳 Chaired a meeting of IT Ministers of States & UTs, IT Secretaries and senior officials alongside MoS Communications Dr. @PemmasaniOnX ji and CM Meghalaya @SangmaConrad ji, to take forward our shared vision of a digitally connected Bharat. From faster Right of Way clearances and Amended BharatNet to last-mile connectivity and stronger action against cyber fraud - discussed how stronger Centre-State synergy can help telecom reach every citizen of India!

— Jyotiraditya M. Scindia (@JM_Scindia) October 8, 2026

item.dc:creator: AYUSH
item.description: AYUSH Women Account for 43% of Overall Ayush Services Workforce; Representation Exceeds 50% Across Several Organised Segments Female Representation Crosses 50% in Hospitals, Day-Care Centres, Educational Institutes and Wellness Establishments Ayush Services Sector Supports 1.76 Million Livelihoods, Emerges as a Significant Engine of Employment and Economic Growth Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 12:33PM by PIB Delhi The Ayush services sector is emerging as an important avenue for women’s participation in the workforce, with female representation exceeding 50 per cent across…
item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
Women Account for 43% of Overall Ayush Services Workforce; Representation Exceeds 50% Across Several Organised Segments
Female Representation Crosses 50% in Hospitals, Day-Care Centres, Educational Institutes and Wellness Establishments
Ayush Services Sector Supports 1.76 Million Livelihoods, Emerges as a Significant Engine of Employment and Economic Growth
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 12:33PM by PIB Delhi

The Ayush services sector is emerging as an important avenue for women’s participation in the workforce, with female representation exceeding 50 per cent across several organised segments, according to a recent assessment of the sector. Women account for 43 per cent of the overall Ayush services workforce, with their representation crossing 50 per cent in hospitals, day-care centres, educational institutes and wellness establishments.

The Ayush services economy, covering Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa and Homoeopathy, was estimated at US$36.92 billion in FY2024-25, registering a robust 16.91 per cent CAGR since FY2022-23. The sector directly supports an estimated 1.76 million livelihoods across healthcare, wellness, education and allied services.

Highlighting the employment potential of the sector, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (IC) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, reiterated, “The growing Ayush services sector is creating meaningful employment opportunities across healthcare, wellness, education and allied services. Its expansion is not only strengthening India’s healthcare ecosystem but also opening new avenues for entrepreneurship, skill development and women’s participation in the workforce.”

According to the Ayush Service Sector Report, a study by RIS released recently on Ayurveda Day 2026, women’s participation is particularly significant across organised Ayush establishments. Female representation exceeds 60 per cent in spas and wellness resorts, stands at 58 per cent in educational institutes, 57 per cent in day-care centres and 53 per cent in hospitals.

The findings highlight the growing role of women across diverse segments of the Ayush services ecosystem, including healthcare delivery, education, wellness and allied services. More than one million livelihoods are concentrated in local and standalone clinics, demonstrating the sector’s extensive employment footprint across urban and rural areas.

Secretary, Ministry of Ayush Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha emphasised, “The expansion of organised Ayush services, supported by quality standards, skilling, digital infrastructure and stronger institutional networks, can significantly enhance both the scale and quality of employment. Greater participation of women in organised Ayush establishments also demonstrates the sector’s potential to contribute to inclusive economic growth.”

Standalone clinics remain the largest revenue-generating segment, contributing an estimated US$16.21 billion, or 43.9 per cent of the sector’s revenue, while day-care centres account for another US$10.13 billion. Together, the two segments contribute more than 70 per cent of the sector’s revenue. Ayurveda remains the largest individual system, accounting for US$17.73 billion, or around 48 per cent of the total Ayush services revenue.

The wellness segment is witnessing particularly strong growth, recording a 21.29 per cent CAGR; meanwhile, Yoga centres registered around 75 per cent revenue growth over two years, reflecting rising demand for preventive health and wellness services.

The sector is also gaining traction in Medical Value Travel (MVT), generating an estimated US$1.77 billion in FY2024-25. International patients, though accounting for around 5 per cent of patient volumes, contribute approximately 15-25 per cent of hospital segment revenue, with therapeutic programmes typically involving stays of 5 to 11 days.

The assessment projects the Ayush services sector to expand from US 36.92 billion in FY 2024–25 to an estimated US 216–318 billion by 2047, with substantial potential to generate employment opportunities across diverse areas, including healthcare delivery, wellness, education, medical travel, research, digital health and allied services.

The growing representation of women across organised Ayush establishments, alongside the sector’s expanding economic and employment footprint, highlights its potential to contribute to women’s economic participation, inclusive growth and India’s broader development journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
India’s regulatory framework for satellite communication services is fair and non-discriminatory
Posted On: 08 OCT 2026 9:19AM by PIB Delhi

A post is being circulated in social media regarding the fairness of India’s regulatory framework for satellite communication services and suggesting that it is being applied in a discriminatory manner. The Government has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite  communication services. Under this, telecom licences have been granted to three Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite services based on non-geosynchronous satellite orbit based satellite communications, as part of its commitment to enable provision of satellite communication services in India. Under the terms and conditions of license, every such licensee is required to demonstrate compliance with security conditions. This is aimed at ensuring that services provided meet various security requirements to ensure safety of all users and their data. Security assessment as part of this process is currently under way in respect of all the three licensees. As and when this process is completed for a licensed entity, it may proceed to the next step of seeking assignment of spectrum. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage. As such, the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived.

***

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister expresses gratitude to President of South Korea Lee Jae-Myung for his wishes on completing 25 years of service to the Nation as Head of Government
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 9:22PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi thanked President of South Korea Lee Jae-Myung for his warm wishes and fondly recalled his visit to India in April, which gave fresh momentum to the India-Republic of Korea Special Strategic Partnership.

The Prime Minister expressed confidence that the two countries will deepen their multifaceted cooperation and continue working together towards global peace, stability and prosperity.

Shri Modi posted on X:

Thank you President Lee Jae-myung for your warm message.

I fondly recall your visit to India in April, which gave fresh momentum to our Special Strategic Partnership.

I am confident that together we will deepen our multifaceted cooperation and advance our shared vision for global peace, stability and prosperity.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister expresses gratitude to Prime Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi for her wishes on completing 25 years of service to the Nation as Head of Government
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 9:16PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi thanked Prime Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi for her warm wishes and recalled her visit to India in July this year, describing it as an unforgettable occasion that further strengthened the India-Japan partnership. The Prime Minister reaffirmed that India and Japan, building on their longstanding friendship, will continue to work together for global peace, stability and prosperity. He expressed confidence that the 75th anniversary of India-Japan diplomatic relations will provide an opportunity to take bilateral ties to new heights.

Shri Modi posted on X:

प्रधानमंत्री ताकाइची जी, आपका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद। 

इस वर्ष जुलाई में हुई आपकी भारत यात्रा मेरे लिए भी अविस्मरणीय रहेगी। इससे भारत-जापान की साझेदारी और सशक्त हुई है। 

दोनों देश अपनी पुरानी मित्रता को और आगे ले जाते हुए वैश्विक शांति, स्थिरता एवं समृद्धि के लिए साथ मिलकर प्रयास करते रहेंगे। 

मुझे विश्वास है कि हमारे राजनयिक संबंधों की 75वीं वर्षगांठ पर द्विपक्षीय रिश्तों को एक नई ऊंचाई मिलेगी।

高市首相、誠にありがとうございました。

今年7月の首相のインド訪問は、私にとっても忘れられないものとなりました。この訪問により、日印のパートナーシップはさらに強固なものとなりました。

両国は、長年にわたる友好関係を基盤として、世界の平和、安定、繁栄のために引き続き協力してまいります。

国交樹立75周年を迎えるにあたり、両国関係が新たな高みに達することを確信しております。

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today thanked the President of India for her wishes and generous words.

These years have been a deeply fulfilling journey of service, shaped at every stage by the affection, faith and blessings of the people.

Whatever progress we have witnessed has been possible because crores of Indians chose to participate in the nation’s transformation with confidence and determination. It is especially heartening to see this change reflected in everyday lives.

item.content:encoded:
Competition Commission of India
CCI approves proposed combination related to internal restructuring of the JSW Group
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 8:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the proposed combination related to internal restructuring of the JSW Group.

The parties to the combination are JSW Steel Limited (JSW Steel), JSW Projects Limited (JSW Projects), and BMM Ispat Limited (BMM).

The Proposed Combination is an internal group restructuring within the JSW Group with the objective of consolidating JSW Group’s majority interest in BMM into full ownership. Currently, JSW Group (through JSW Projects) holds 58.47% equity shareholding in BMM, and BMM is commercially integrated within JSW Group’s supply chain through intra-group sales and procurements. With the intent to enhance operational, financial, and organisational efficiencies through economies of scale, resource pooling, and rationalisation of capital, JSW Group proposes to fully absorb BMM by way of an amalgamation into JSW Steel.

JSW Steel, listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and BSE Limited, is primarily engaged in the manufacture and sale of a diverse range of iron and steel products in India and abroad and forms part of the JSW Group. With fully integrated operations spanning across mining, raw material processing, steel production and downstream value-added manufacturing.

JSW Projects is an unlisted public limited company headquartered at Mumbai, and forms part of the JSW Group. JSW Projects is engaged in the business of manufacturing iron ore pellets, Sponge Iron / DRI, and power generation for captive use, which are ultimately used in the manufacture of steel and steel products only for JSW Steel.

BMM, a public limited company incorporated in India, is a steel manufacturing company engaged in producing semi-finished and long steel products and operates an approximately 1 MTPA integrated steel manufacturing facility in Karnataka.

As an integrated facility, BMM undertakes the full steelmaking process, from ironmaking through to finished long-product rolling, within its Karnataka plant.

item.content:encoded:
Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of certain shareholding in Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited by CPP Investment Board Pvt. Holdings (4) Inc.
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 7:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of  India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of certain shareholding in Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited by CPP Investment Board Private Holdings (4) Inc.

The Proposed Combination envisages acquisition of certain shareholding in Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited (Target) by CPP Investment Board Private Holdings (4) Inc. (Acquirer).

The Acquirer is incorporated in Canada and is managed by Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB) which is a professional investment management organisation that manages the Canada Pension Plan Fund. In order to build a diversified portfolio of assets, it makes investments around the world in public equities, private equities, real estate, infrastructure, fixed income and alternative strategies, including in partnership with funds.

The Target is a public limited company, incorporated in India, and forms part of the Prestige group. The Target is primarily engaged in owning and developing luxury, upper upscale, upscale and upper midscale hospitality assets in India, including operating, ongoing and upcoming hotels and serviced apartments for business and leisure travellers.

item.content:encoded:
Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of sole control over Omega-Meyer Ltd and Meyer Organics by BCPE Wellbeing Holdco Two Ltd. and Integral Investments Asia IV Ltd
Acquirers, BCPE Wellbeing Holdco Two Ltd. and Integral Investments Asia IV Ltd are funds managed/ advised by Bain Capital
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 7:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of sole control over Omega-Meyer Limited and Meyer Organics Private Limited by BCPE Wellbeing Holdco Two Limited and Integral Investments Asia IV Limited, which are funds managed and/ or advised by Bain Capital.

The Proposed Combination relates to acquisition of sole control over Omega-Meyer Limited (Cyan Target) and Meyer Organics Private Limited (Meyer Target), which own and control the group of companies and affiliates doing business as ‘Vitabiotics’ and ‘Meyer Organics’ respectively, by funds managed and/ or advised by Bain Capital Investors, LLC (Bain Capital) acting through BCPE Wellbeing Holdco Two Limited (Acquirer 1) and Integral Investments Asia IV Limited (Acquirer 2).

Bain Capital is a private equity investment firm based in the USA that invests in companies across a number of industries, including information technology, healthcare, retail and consumer products, communications, financial services and industrial/ manufacturing.

The Targets are engaged in provision of nutraceuticals globally as well as in India. Meyer Organics Private Limited also has presence in production and supply of some over-the-counter and prescription finished dose pharmaceuticals in India.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Central Zoo Authority (CZA) and Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM) inaugurate 3-Day Regional Training Programme for Zookeepers at IIFM, Bhopal
To facilitate Uniform Welfare Standards and enhance Coordination between Zookeepers and Zoo Management in Central India
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 7:48PM by PIB Delhi

A three-day regional training programme for Zoo Keepers of zoos in Central India commenced today at the Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM), Bhopal. Organized jointly by the Central Zoo Authority (CZA) and IIFM from 7th - 9th October, 2026, the programme aims to strengthen the professional capacities of zoo keepers in captive animal care, behaviour, facility operations, and conservation education.

One of the functions of the Central Zoo Authority under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 is to co-ordinate training of zoo personnel. Recognizing that zookeepers form the operational backbone of zoological parks and are directly responsible for daily animal management this regional initiative provides both technical classroom sessions and hands-on field visit at Van Vihar National Park, Bhopal.

In his inaugural address, Director (IIFM), Dr. K. Ravichandran, recognized zookeepers as the frontline foundation of daily zoo operations, noting that the success of zoo management ultimately rests on their hands-on dedication. He emphasized that grounding keepers in structured technical training and safety protocols boosts overall operational efficiency, lowers on-the-job risks, and strengthens the role of zoos in conservation education.

Addressing the session, Member Secretary (CZA), Dr. V. Clement Ben, emphasized that animal keepers are at the heart of zoo management, as their daily vigilance provides the earliest indicators of an animal's health and welfare. Modern zookeeping requires continuous learning, strict safety practices, and disciplined record-keeping. He urged keepers to treat safety as a daily culture and foster close teamwork with veterinarians and managers, reminding them that their daily work directly shapes animal welfare, operational safety, and conservation outcomes.

The initiative seeks to establish uniform welfare standards and enhance coordination between zookeepers and zoo management across zoos in Central India.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NCSC Intervention Results in Mandatory Reporting of SC Beneficiaries under Key Financial Schemes
Mandatory Scheme-wise and Bank-wise Reporting of SC Beneficiaries Directed by Department of Financial Services
Directions Issued to SLBC/UTLBC Convenors Across States and Union Territories; Action-Taken Report to be Submitted by October 9, 2026
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 7:28PM by PIB Delhi

Following the intervention of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, has issued directions for mandatory reporting of assistance provided to Scheduled Caste beneficiaries under major government financial schemes.

Under the directions, State Level Bankers’ Committees (SLBCs) and UTLBCs have been advised to include scheme-wise and bank-wise details of the number and percentage of Scheduled Caste beneficiaries assisted under the identified schemes in their periodic review meetings.

They have also been directed to regularly share the information with the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and submit an action-taken report to the Department of Financial Services by October 9, 2026, including details regarding data availability and any issues in compilation.

The Department of Financial Services has further directed that the reporting should be undertaken using data already available with banks and implementing agencies. This will ensure consistency in definitions and methodology without creating parallel reporting requirements. SLBCs and UTLBCs have also been asked to furnish an update on the action taken within 30 days.

On September 24, 2026, Secretary, NCSC, Shri Vivek Kumar Dewangan, wrote to the Secretary, Department of Financial Services, highlighting that State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) reports were not reflecting the percentage of Scheduled Caste families and beneficiaries assisted under major government schemes, including Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), Stand-Up India, Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), PM SVANidhi, CGTMSE and MSME Business Loans.

The Commission had pointed out that the absence of such data was hindering the discharge of its Constitutional mandate under Article 338(5)(c) to evaluate the progress of socio-economic development of Scheduled Castes. In response, the Department of Financial Services issued directions dated October 5, 2026 to all SLBC/UTLBC Convenors across States and Union Territories.

The directions are expected to significantly strengthen transparency and accountability in the delivery of financial inclusion benefits to Scheduled Caste communities. Availability of scheme-wise and bank-wise data will enable the National Commission for Scheduled Castes to more effectively discharge its Constitutional responsibilities and assess the progress of socio-economic development of Scheduled Castes.

Shri Dewangan said the National Commission for Scheduled Castes will continue to monitor the implementation of these directions and remain engaged with stakeholders to ensure that the benefits of government schemes reach the intended Scheduled Caste beneficiaries in a measurable and equitable manner.

item.category: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
item.description: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways PM Narendra Modi calls for Rules-Based Maritime Order in Message to 3rd Sagarmanthan Dialogue Prime Minister welcomes Global Leaders to the Thought Leadership Conference, cites Port Growth & New Maritime Laws India's maritime vision extends across regions and oceans and is built on cooperation, trust, mutual respect and mutual benefit: PM Modi Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 7:18PM by PIB Delhi Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed policymakers, maritime leaders and experts from around the world to the third edition of Sagarmanthan: The…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
PM Narendra Modi calls for Rules-Based Maritime Order in Message to 3rd Sagarmanthan Dialogue
Prime Minister welcomes Global Leaders to the Thought Leadership Conference, cites Port Growth & New Maritime Laws
India's maritime vision extends across regions and oceans and is built on cooperation, trust, mutual respect and mutual benefit: PM Modi
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 7:18PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed policymakers, maritime leaders and experts from around the world to the third edition of Sagarmanthan: The Great Oceans Dialogue on Tuesday, calling for a "free, open, secure and rules-based maritime order" that brings peace and prosperity to all nations.

"Our vision is of a free, open, secure and rules-based maritime order that brings greater peace, prosperity and progress for all. I am confident that Sagarmanthan will give greater strength to this larger vision," PM Modi said in a written message to the conference, which the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) and the Observer Research Foundation (ORF) are organising in New Delhi.

PM Modi said what happens in one part of the world can affect places far beyond its shores, making global dialogue and cooperation on the oceans more important than ever. The name Sagarmanthan, which means "churning of the ocean," holds special meaning in Indian tradition, where the churning is linked to the discovery of new possibilities, Modi said. He said the oceans hold "immense promise" for the world's economies, people and planet.

“India's relationship with the ocean is also about responsibility. As we build a stronger maritime economy, we are protecting the health of our oceans and coastal ecosystems. India's maritime vision extends across regions and oceans and is built on cooperation, trust, mutual respect and mutual benefit. We believe the oceans must become a source of shared prosperity, where every country has a voice and an opportunity to grow,” wrote Prime Minister.

Modi traced India's seafaring history from the ancient port city of Lothal to the Chola dynasty and the naval vision of Maratha ruler Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Indian sailors and traders carried goods, ideas, stories and culture to distant lands, he said. PM Modi linked the country's maritime ambitions to Viksit Bharat, the government's goal of making India a developed nation by 2047.

PM Modi said India's major ports have nearly doubled their capacity while turnaround times have dropped significantly. “India is looking at the sea with a renewed sense of purpose. The journey towards Viksit Bharat by 2047 is also a journey towards a stronger and more capable maritime India. We are preparing for a new era of shipbuilding and green shipping. Our major ports have nearly doubled their capacity, while turnaround times have come down significantly,” said PM Modi.

The government is also investing in ocean science and exploration to better understand the country's seas and use them responsibly. “India has also brought in new-generation maritime laws to create a modern framework for the sector. At the same time, we are investing in ocean science and exploration so that we can understand our seas better and make responsible use of their immense potential,” added PM Modi.

Modi said Indian seafarers now form the second-largest maritime workforce in the world, with young Indians earning respect across the world's oceans. He said India is protecting ocean health and coastal ecosystems as it builds a stronger maritime economy. India's maritime vision rests on cooperation, trust, mutual respect and mutual benefit, he said.

"We believe the oceans must become a source of shared prosperity, where every country has a voice and an opportunity to grow," PM Modi said. He expressed confidence that Sagarmanthan would strengthen that vision and said he hoped the dialogue would bring fresh ideas, deeper partnerships and opportunities for generations to come.

The meeting was chaired by…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
DDWS Organised Regional Review Meeting of States/UTs under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 at IIM Bangalore
Secretary, DDWS urges States to strengthen source sustainability, water quality surveillance and service delivery under JJM 2.0
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 7:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised a regional review meeting of States and Union Territories under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIM Bangalore) today. The meeting was chaired by Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, in the presence of Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), and attended by senior officials from States and UTs. The meeting reviewed the progress of JJM 2.0 and discussed key reform measures relating to source sustainability, water quality surveillance, digital governance, community participation and long-term sustainability of rural water supply systems.

In his opening address, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena emphasised that Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 marks a significant shift from infrastructure creation to sustainable and accountable service delivery. He urged States and UTs to accelerate implementation of approved schemes and effectively utilise available resources while ensuring that investments are directed towards fully functional schemes delivering reliable drinking water services to rural households. Stressing the importance of outcomes-based implementation, he underlined that expenditure must be translated into functional infrastructure supported by complete source-to-household connectivity, robust digital records and effective monitoring systems.

Secretary Shri Meena highlighted that Jal Jeevan Mission has transformed rural drinking water access across the country, with more than 15.96 crore rural households now having tap water connections compared to only 3.27 crore households at the time of the Mission's launch in August 2019. He noted that the focus of JJM 2.0 is on sustaining these gains through source sustainability, financial and operational efficiency, water quality assurance and citizen-centric service delivery.

Shri Meena called upon States to expedite implementation of both single-village and multi-village water supply schemes, particularly in quality-affected areas, and ensure timely utilisation of available resources. Referring to the decisions taken during recent sectoral deliberations on water governance, he urged States and UTs to establish effective mechanisms for monitoring and implementing agreed reform measures to further strengthen service delivery under JJM 2.0.

Highlighting findings emerging from Jal Seva Adhayan, he observed that pipeline leakages and breakages continue to be the leading cause of water supply disruptions, followed by power cuts and low-voltage related challenges. He emphasised the need for States to adopt both immediate and long-term solutions to improve the reliability of rural water supply systems and ensure uninterrupted drinking water services to rural households.

The Secretary further underscored the importance of exploring renewable energy solutions for rural drinking water infrastructure. He informed that discussions are underway with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) to examine the solarisation of drinking water assets across the country. He noted that innovative approaches leveraging solar energy can reduce operational costs, improve service reliability and strengthen the long-term sustainability of rural drinking water systems.

Addressing the participants, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM, highlighted the importance of addressing operational challenges affecting rural water supply schemes. Referring to findings emerging from Jal Seva Adhayan and related assessments, he noted that low voltage and poor power quality continue to impact service delivery in several areas. He emphasised that reducing power-related costs can significantly improve operational sustainability and urged States and UTs to work collectively towards identifying practical solutions for improving energy efficiency and reducing recurring operation and maintenance expenditure.

Prof. Gopal Naik, JJM Professor Chair, IIM Bangalore, presented a study titled “Power Cost Optimization in JJM Scheme”. The study examined various energy configurations for rural water supply systems, including grid-based and solar-powered models, and assessed their implications on operational and life-cycle costs. The presentation highlighted opportunities for reducing recurring operation and maintenance expenditure, improving affordability of water services and enhancing the financial sustainability of rural water supply schemes through innovative energy solutions.

The programme also featured presentations on research related to drinking water quality monitoring and management using Water Quality Management Information System (WQMIS) data. The findings indicated significant improvements in drinking water quality compliance across several parameters following implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission and highlighted opportunities for strengthening laboratory ecosystems, independent surveillance mechanisms and community-led water quality management.

During the discussions, Secretary, DDWS emphasised the importance of establishing independent water quality surveillance mechanisms to strengthen transparency and accountability in rural water supply systems. He underscored the need to make water quality information available to Gram Panchayats and communities and highlighted the role of Gram Sabhas in reviewing water quality findings and identifying remedial measures. He noted that community participation and data-driven decision-making will be critical for improving long-term service delivery outcomes under JJM 2.0.

During the review meeting, States and UTs also discussed progress on key JJM 2.0 priorities, including State Implementation Plans, financial reconciliation, Har Ghar Jal certification in PM-JANMAN villages, Jal Arpan, digital governance initiatives and water quality management. The meeting concluded with States and UTs sharing progress, challenges and best practices and reaffirming their commitment to advancing the Mission's vision of sustainable water security through cooperative federalism, technology-enabled governance and Jan Bhagidari.

In his concluding remarks, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM urged State/UTs to accelerate implementation of key reform initiatives under JJM 2.0. Referring to Jal Arpan, the formal handing over of schemes to GP and VWSC he emphasised the need to complete in all Har Ghar Jal villages and ensure generation of certificates in the approved regional languages.

Shri Soan further called upon State/UTs to expedite water quality testing, particularly in Anganwadi Centres and other public institutions and ensure timely uploading of test results on the designated digital platforms. He urged to operationalise the O&M Manual at the Gram Panchayat level, actively utilise the Decision Support System (DSS) for source sustainability planning and monitoring, and strengthen coordination with Panchayati Raj Institutions for effective management of rural water supply systems. He also emphasised timely submission of inputs on DSS, completion of capacity-building activities, adherence to Finance Commission compliance requirements and preparation of clear implementation plans for achieving JJM 2.0 reform milestones.

***

Financial assistance can play an important role in helping individuals from disadvantaged communities establish sustainable livelihoods and improve their economic condition. Mr. Raghubir Singh,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Strong Financial Assistance and Steps Towards Self-Reliance
Punjab’s Raghubir Singh's Journey towards Economic Self-Reliance
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:57PM by PIB Delhi

Timely support for self-employment can provide the means to strengthen existing enterprises, increase income opportunities and move towards greater financial stability. Financial assistance can play an important role in helping individuals from disadvantaged communities establish sustainable livelihoods and improve their economic condition.

Mr. Raghubir Singh, aged 43, from Punjab, received financial assistance of Rs. 2.50 lakh in 2025 under the NSFDC Term Loan Scheme. The financial assistance enabled him to install modern machines and expand his tailoring and embroidery business, thereby strengthening his existing livelihood and creating better opportunities for income generation.

Before availing the assistance, Mr. Singh's monthly income was Rs. 10,000. With the expansion of his business and effective utilisation of the financial support, his monthly income increased to approximately Rs. 20,000. The increase in income has strengthened his financial position and enabled him to meet his household needs in a more stable and secure manner.

The loan assistance has significantly improved Mr. Singh's economic condition and provided him with an opportunity to pursue self-employment with greater financial stability. By making regular repayments of the loan, he has demonstrated financial discipline while continuing to strengthen his tailoring and embroidery business.

Shri Raghubir Singh expressed his satisfaction and said, “The financial assistance helped me expand my tailoring and embroidery business and increase my monthly income. It has strengthened my financial position and enabled me to move towards greater self-reliance."

Mr. Raghubir Singh's journey demonstrates how timely financial assistance can enable individuals to expand their enterprises, improve their earning capacity and move towards economic self-reliance. His experience reflects the role of NSFDC's financial support in creating sustainable livelihood opportunities and promoting a stronger and more self-reliant society.

SS-120-NSFDC-RS
