item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
PMGSY Chintan Shivir Charts Future Roadmap for Quality, Maintenance and Technology-Driven Rural Connectivity
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Calls for Greater Use of Technology to Strengthen PMGSY and Ensure Last-Mile Rural Connectivity
PMGSY Chintan Shivir Emphasises Climate-Resilient Infrastructure, Sustainable Practices and Faster Delivery of Rural Roads
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:54PM by PIB Delhi

The two-day Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) Chintan Shivir was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 5–6 October 2026, bringing together senior officers and representatives from States/UTs, policymakers, technical experts, Knowledge partners and other stakeholders to deliberate upon future action taken for strengthening rural road connectivity through PMGSY.

Over the past 25 years, PMGSY has emerged as a transformative programme for rural connectivity, with around 8 lakh km of rural roads constructed under different phases of the programme. Under PMGSY-IV, with an outlay of ₹70,125 crore, around 62,500 km of all-weather roads are targeted to provide connectivity to 25,000 eligible unconnected habitations.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chauhan, Union Minister of Rural Development and Agriculture and Farmers Welfare of  India addressed the Chintan Shivir for greater focus on new technologies and connectivity to each eligible habitation. Union Minsiter has emphasised the importance of a pakka road which not only gives connectivity but also opens the doors of many opportunities. He also emphasized greater use of digital technologies, GPS-based monitoring and Artificial Intelligence (AI) for field verification, monitoring and timely decision-making. He has also pressed upon overcoming of challenges faced during implementation using guidnace of doamin experts and policy makers. 

Addressing the Chintan Shivir, the Hon’ble Union Minister of Rural Development emphasized the need for timely completion of ongoing works, expeditious preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) and tendering, improved construction quality, preventive maintenance and stronger accountability at all levels.

Shri Kamlesh Paswan, Hon’ble Minister of State for Rural Development highlighted the need for close monitoring of pending and delayed works, particularly in difficult and North-Eastern areas. He emphasized stronger contractor responsibility during the stipulated five-year maintenance period, examination of genuine connectivity gaps under PMGSY-IV and improved coordination among stakeholders for timely resolution of implementation constraints. He also urged state to timely complet works and adopt green technologies in construction of PMGSY works.

Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Rural Development, apprised the gathering of the new initiatives incorporated under PMGSY to further support the existing system and strengthen it through a transparent mechanism. He also urged implementing States/UTs to quickly adopt these tools and maximise the use of new technology, which will improve the quality of construction and assist the Ministry in analysing and resolving issues.

Secreatary, Rural Development stressed upon timely completion of set targets to deliver all weatehr roads. Maintenance and quality are non-negotiable aspects under the scheme. He urged all seniors represenattives from state to work in mission mode with proper action plan for better delivery. He has mentioend about the milestones achieved under the scheme however, pushed for next milestones.

The Secretary, Rural Development, extended his warm greetings and congratulations to all participants who have joined the Chintan Shivir from across the country. He appreciated their presence and active participation in this important forum and acknowledged their valuable role in the implementation of this significant scheme. He emphasised that the collective experience, commitment and contributions of all stakeholders would be instrumental in further strengthening the scheme and achieving its objectives.

Expert sessions/deliberations on future-ready rural roads

1.         The Chintan Shivir also featured expert discussions from CRRI. NDMA,CDRI on disaster- and climate-resilient rural roads, emerging construction technologies, sustainable materials and AI-enabled digital monitoring systems. The deliberations focused on identifying proven practices and innovative solutions that can be scaled up for field-level implementation across the country.

2.         Learning from the rich field experience of an expert officer from the Border Roads Organisation (BRO), who shared valuable insights into constructing roads in some of the country’s most challenging and difficult terrains. The innovative practices, technical solutions and lessons from BRO’s experience can offer important learnings for PMGSY, particularly for road construction in hilly, remote and border areas.

Key takeaways from delibeartions and expert discussion emerging from the Chintan Shivir

  • Promoting climate-resilient, sustainable and locally appropriate designs, materials and construction technologies.
  • Leveraging OMMAS, GPS-VTS, AI, geo-tagged evidence and data analytics for transparent, outcome-based monitoring and maintenance.
  • Strengthening accountability and coordination among the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA) and States/UTs.
  • Timely completion of ongoing works and accelerated progress in lagging States/UTs.
  • Expeditious preparation and processing of PMGSY-IV DPRs, including associated bridge DPRs, and addressing eligible connectivity gaps.
  • Strengthening the sanction-to-tender-to-award cycle through better pre-tender preparedness and timely clearances.
  • Placing quality assurance, preventive maintenance and field verification at the core of implementation.

 

The Chintan Shivir reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to building quality, sustainable, climate-resilient and technology-enabled rural road infrastructure that delivers lasting socio-economic benefits to rural communities.

Rural roads are not merely infrastructure for transportation; they are vital links connecting farmers to markets, children to educational institutions, patients to healthcare services and rural families to new opportunities.

Strengthening rural connectivity is therefore an important pathway towards the vision of a Viksit Bharat, with a strong, prosperous and well-connected rural India at its foundation.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP) notifies regulations for autonomous boards and central assessment committee to strengthen quality, transparency and standardisation in allied and healthcare education
Autonomous Boards to strengthen quality assessment and standards in allied and healthcare institutions
NCAHP notifies competency based Diploma in Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology curriculum under One Nation One Curriculum
Two-year D.MRIT programme to include six-month clinical internship in radiology and imaging
NCAHP introduces digital registration with Unique Identification numbers and QR-coded certificates for allied and healthcare professionals
State and Central Registers to enable public verification of allied and healthcare professionals
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi

The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, has notified measures under the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021 to strengthen standards in allied and healthcare education and professional practice. These include the Autonomous Boards and Central Assessment Committee (Establishment, Constitution, Functions and Powers) Regulations, 2026, the competency-based curriculum for the Diploma in Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology (D.MRIT) and the Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026.

 

The measures provide for institutional assessment and quality assurance, competency-based education and training and a structured system for registration and verification of allied and healthcare professionals.

 

Strengthening institutional standards through Autonomous Boards and Central Assessment Committee

 

The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP) has notified the following regulations – (a) Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026 (b) Autonomous Boards and Central Assessment Committee (Establishment, Constitution, Functions and Powers) Regulations, 2026, under the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021. The Regulations provide a framework for strengthening institutional assessment, quality assurance and implementation of standards for recognised courses.

 

Salient Features of the Regulations

 

  • The Regulations provide for the establishment and functioning of Autonomous Boards under State Allied and Healthcare Councils, with defined responsibilities for education, institutional assessment, professional ethics and registration. The Autonomous Boards will have 10 to 20 members, including a President, with representation from recognised allied and healthcare professional categories.
  • The Undergraduate and Postgraduate Boards will facilitate implementation of standards for recognised courses, competency-based frameworks, faculty development, training and research, and will submit reports and recommendations to the State Council.
  • The Assessment and Rating Board will evaluate applications for recognition and Letters of Permission, undertake institutional inspections, review annual disclosures, empanel assessors, assess and rate institutions, and make assessment and rating information available in the public domain through the State Council website.
  • The Ethics and Registration Board will verify the documents of professionals and recommend for registration. The Board will support the maintenance of the State registers and the implementation of professional ethics and conduct standards, and will evaluate complaints and violations and make recommendations concerning professional registration.

 

Central Assessment Committee (CAC)

 

  • For States where a functional State Council does not exist, the Regulations provide for a Central Assessment Committee (CAC) under the overall supervision of NCAHP and assisted by the NCAHP Secretariat. The CAC will perform the functions of Autonomous Boards and follow the prescribed verification, inspection and rating procedures.
  • The CAC will comprise 10 to 30 members, including a President, with representation from professional categories and additional representation, where required, to ensure appropriate State and Union Territory coverage, particularly for areas without functional State Councils.
  • The Regulations also prescribe grounds and due process for removal of CAC members, including conflict of interest, breach of code, abuse of position and other specified circumstances, with an opportunity of hearing.

 

Towards Standardised and Quality driven Allied and Healthcare Education

 

  • The NCAHP had previously notified the Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026, enabling allied and healthcare professionals to register under the Act and practice their profession. The notification of these regulations ensures a seamless and transparent registration process in Central and State registers.
  • By establishing clearly defined institutional assessment, inspection and rating mechanisms, together with dedicated functions for education, ethics and registration, the Regulations provide a structured framework for improving the quality of education and professional standards in the allied and healthcare sector.

 

Competency-based education to meet growing demand for trained imaging professionals

 

With the objective of standardising education and training, NCAHP has notified the competency-based curriculum for the Diploma in Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology (D.MRIT) on 30th September 2026 under One Nation One Curriculum for the Allied and Healthcare sector.

Institutions imparting or intending to impart the D.MRIT course must mandatorily adopt the curriculum from the academic year 2027–28. Institutes desiring to implement it during the academic year 2026–27 may adopt the curriculum from that academic year.

The Diploma programme has been developed keeping in view the growing requirement for trained professionals in Medical Radiology and Imaging services at Primary Health Centres (PHCs), hospitals, diagnostic centres and other healthcare facilities. There has also been demand from students and stakeholders for an appropriate diploma-level programme in the field of Radiology and Imaging.

The D.MRIT is a two-year programme for students who have completed Class 12 in the Science stream with Physics, Chemistry and Biology (PCB) from a recognised Board or equivalent. The curriculum represents a transition from traditional, knowledge-oriented education towards a competency-based approach, with emphasis on the acquisition of Knowledge, Skills, Values and Attitudes required for safe, effective and ethical practice in Medical Radiology and Imaging services.

An important component of the programme is a six-month internship, designed to provide students with structured hands-on clinical exposure and opportunities to apply theoretical knowledge in real-world healthcare settings. The internship will facilitate the development of practical skills, professional competencies, patient-care practices, radiation safety practices and familiarity with imaging procedures and equipment under appropriate supervision.

The curriculum is designed to ensure that professionals completing the programme acquire the requisite theoretical knowledge, practical skills and professional competencies to function in Medical Radiology and Imaging and contribute effectively to diagnostic services such as X-rays, CT Scan, Sonography, Mammography and Fluoroscopy, while adhering to prescribed standards of patient safety, radiation protection, quality assurance and professional practice.

The notification of the Diploma programme complements the competency-based education framework already established by the Commission for higher levels of education in the discipline. The Bachelor of Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology (B.MRIT) and Master of Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology (M.MRIT) competency-based curricula were earlier released by the Commission vide notice dated 24th April 2025, for implementation from the academic year 2026–27.

The introduction of the D.MRIT curriculum alongside the existing Bachelor’s and Master’s programmes provides a structured educational pathway in Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology and is aimed at supporting the availability of appropriately trained professionals while promoting uniformity, standardisation and quality in Allied and Healthcare education across the country.

The Commission has so far released 20 competency-based curricula across various Allied and Healthcare Professions. These curricula have been developed with the objective of strengthening competency-based education, standardising training and ensuring that students acquire the knowledge, skills and professional attributes required for contemporary healthcare delivery.

Registration framework to strengthen transparency and verification of professionals

The Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026, notified by NCAHP and published in the Gazette of India on 15th September 2026, establish a comprehensive framework for registration of allied and healthcare professionals in both the State Registers and the Central Register, along with issuance of certificates of registration with Unique Identification (UID) numbers through an online system.

A person will be entitled to practise a recognised allied and healthcare profession only after obtaining registration in accordance with the Regulations. Eligibility requires holding a recognised primary qualification. Professionals residing in a State or Union Territory where a functional State Council has not yet been established may register directly with the Central Register.

Registration will remain valid for five years and may be renewed upon fulfilment of Continuing Professional Development (CPD) requirements through approved online and offline modes.

The Regulations provide for real-time synchronisation between the State Registers and the Central Register through an integrated online system. The Central and State Registers will be accessible to the public through the websites of the Commission and the respective State Councils, displaying prescribed particulars of registered professionals and enabling verification of registration status.

Every registered professional will be issued a Unique Identification (UID) number through the centralised system. Registration certificates, including digital certificates featuring the UID and a secure QR code, will be issued by the Commission or the respective State Council, facilitating identification and verification of registered professionals.

The Regulations also provide for interim registration for students enrolled in recognised institutions who are undertaking internships, clinical training, observerships or practical coursework required to complete an allied and healthcare qualification. Interim registration must be initiated by the recognised institution and obtained from the concerned State Council, with no fee charged for interim registration applications.

The Regulations establish a pathway for Indian citizens holding foreign qualifications in allied and healthcare. A foreign-qualified allied and healthcare professional will be eligible to apply for registration where the qualification is recognised by the Commission or the prescribed credential equivalency evaluation has been completed, along with the relevant exit examination where applicable. Temporary registration is also provided for eligible foreign-qualified Indian professionals for specific, time-bound purposes including postgraduate or specialty education, fellowships, clinical research, observerships, advanced workshops, expert visits and voluntary community service.

The Regulations permit temporary registration for sponsored foreign professionals for specific, timebound purposes. They also provide for Good Standing Certificates for registered allied and healthcare professionals pursuing foreign education, carrying out professional activities or participating in student exchange programmes outside India.

The Commission is undertaking efforts to introduce provisional registration for professionals currently practising in the allied and healthcare sector who lack the prescribed primary qualifications. Such professionals will be provided an option to undergo a bridge course to attain eligibility for regular registration.

The registration and payment of fee will be processed through an online portal, supporting a more streamlined registration process and greater transparency in the allied and healthcare workforce.

Taken together, these measures strengthen standards in allied and healthcare education and professional practice through institutional assessment, competency-based training and a transparent system of professional registration and verification.

The framework seeks to support quality education and training and enable patients and service users to verify the registration of allied and healthcare professionals.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development to be held in New Delhi on 8-9 October
Summit to bring together Centre and States to deliberate on key priorities concerning nutrition, child protection, women’s safety and empowerment
Summit to focus on four key areas covering Anganwadi Centres, protection of vulnerable children, women’s safety and women’s empowerment
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards realizing the vision of a Suposhit, Surakshit and Sashakt Bharat as the foundation for Viksit Bharat@2047, the Ministry of Women and Child Development will host its Departmental Summit on 8th and 9th October 2026 at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, New Delhi. The Summit is the second in the series of Departmental Summits envisioned by Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi to strengthen cooperative federalism, foster collective ownership of national priorities, and accelerate outcomes through closer Centre-State collaboration.

The Departmental Summit model brings together political leadership and senior officials from the Union and State Governments to deliberate on sectoral priorities, share good practices, address implementation challenges, and agree on time-bound actions for improved governance and service delivery.

The two-day Summit will focus on four themes:

  • Reimagining Anganwadi Centres for better nutrition and early education
  • Strengthening the protection system for vulnerable children
  • Women safety through effective implementation of institutional and legislative frameworks
  • Women empowerment through enhancing the effectiveness and outcomes of key schemes.

First-day discussions will cover the quality of Take-Home Ration and Hot Cooked Meals, Poshan Tracker data quality improvement, Early Childhood Care and Education, protection systems for vulnerable children including the impact of social media, and implementation challenges and solutions for women safety. The second day will be devoted to enhancing the effectiveness and outcomes of key schemes for women empowerment.

Participating States will share their experiences, challenges and their best practices, and try to arrive at consensus on agreed outcomes, reinforcing spirit of cooperative federalism and shared responsibility. The key outcomes and action plans to achieve these will be presented before the Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, during the valedictory session. The Prime Minister's guidance is expected to galvanise the collective resolve of the Centre and States and set the course for decisive and time-bound action on the agreed outcomes.

***

RC/PC

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Steel
Ministry of Steel Organises Mini Chintan Shivir on ‘Peace of Mind at Workplace’
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Steel organised a Mini ChintanShivir on the theme ‘Peace of Mind at Workplace’ today at the Civil Services Officers’ Institute (CSOI), Chanakyapuri, New Delhi. The session aimed to encourage officers and employees to create a stress-free work environment and build emotional strength. Brahma Kumari Sister Shivani, a well-known spiritual speaker, was the chief guest and keynote speaker at the event.

Addressing the gathering at the beginning of the programme, the Secretary, Ministry of Steel, Shri Sandeep Poundrik, emphasised that maintaining peace of mind at the workplace is important as it also helps improve productivity and efficiency.

Speaking on the theme, Sister Shivani urged officers and employees to focus on reducing stress and developing a positive outlook. She said that when we make a firm resolve to achieve something, we can move towards accomplishing it, and the same approach can also be applied to managing stress. She stressed the importance of maintaining a positive outlook in every situation.

Highlighting the power of Sankalp (Resolution), Sister Shivani said that when a resolution is repeated again and again, it begins to influence our lives. The more we think about and repeat something, the more it shapes our thoughts and behaviour. Therefore, it is important to be mindful that our thoughts and resolutions remain positive. She said that this is the principle of ‘Sankalp Se Siddhi’, which can take our society and the country forward on the path of progress.

***

Aman

item.title: 5th Meeting of Live Events Development Cell Reviews Single-Window Clearances and Next-Gen Reforms for Live Events Sector
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 5th Meeting of Live Events Development Cell Reviews Single-Window Clearances and Next-Gen Reforms for Live Events Sector India’s Live Events Sector Grows 44% in One Year, Supports Over One Crore Livelihoods Government Targets Doubling of Live Events Sector by 2030 through Centre-State-Industry Collaboration States and UTs Urged to Route End-to-End Live Event Licensing through India Cine Hub Portal Single National Music Licence, Notified Entertainment Zones and Infrastructure Status for Live Event Venues Discussed Posted On: 07 OCT…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
5th Meeting of Live Events Development Cell Reviews Single-Window Clearances and Next-Gen Reforms for Live Events Sector
India’s Live Events Sector Grows 44% in One Year, Supports Over One Crore Livelihoods
Government Targets Doubling of Live Events Sector by 2030 through Centre-State-Industry Collaboration
States and UTs Urged to Route End-to-End Live Event Licensing through India Cine Hub Portal
Single National Music Licence, Notified Entertainment Zones and Infrastructure Status for Live Event Venues Discussed
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Shri Chanchal Kumar, said today that India’s live events sector grew by 44 per cent over the past year, with around 34,000 events held across the country and the sector now supporting more than one crore livelihoods. Addressing the 5th meeting of the Live Events Development Cell (LEDC), he said the Government has set an ambitious target of doubling the sector by 2030, with the potential to generate 15–20 million direct and ancillary jobs. He described the LEDC as “one of the finest examples of cooperation between industry, States and the Centre”.

Shri Chanchal Kumar highlighted the LEDC brings together 14 Central Ministries and Departments, 10 States and UTs and 21 industry bodies, and has taken forward key reforms including the Model Executive Order, Single Window Portal on India Cine Hub, streamlined clearances and skilling initiatives. He noted that the number of States and UTs with designated Nodal Officers has increased from 16 to 29.

The meeting reviewed the implementation of the Single Window Clearances Portal for the live event industry on the India Cine Hub (ICH) portal. States and UTs were asked to designate Nodal Officers, nominate authorised officers from departments, integrate departmental and local licensing systems with the ICH Portal, route the complete licence lifecycle through the portal, onboard live event venues and notify live event licensing as a time-bound public service.

Further, it was informed that five States have so far adopted the “Model Executive Order for Streamlining Licensing and Permissions for Live Events in India, 2026”, which was shared with States and Union Territories on 13th March 2026. The state of Maharashtra, (LEDC member State) has adopted the MEO and made a presentation on its implementation. The remaining States and Union Territories were urged to expedite adoption. It was also informed that the Ministry of Home Affairs has streamlined FRRO re-registration requirements for short-term stays by foreign performers.

Central Ministries were requested to take forward sector-specific facilitation, including group visa provisions for artists and crews with customs duty exemption for show equipment by the concerned ministries; integration of live entertainment skills into the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF), training and certification centres and apprenticeship programmes by the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship; promotion of India as a global hub for event-based tourism by the Ministry of Tourism; and financial incentives including GST rationalisation and CSR alignment, infrastructure financing through VGF and blended finance, and recognition of the live entertainment sector under MSME by the respective ministries.

Further, the LEDC deliberated on next-generation reforms, including a single national music licence with notified tariffs to replace overlapping demands from multiple rights societies, notified entertainment precincts under the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000, and relaxation of caps on foreign remittances for payments to international artists.

On pre-approved venues, it was informed that the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and the Sports Authority of India (SAI) have issued SOPs for organising live events at their assets, and major venues are to be pre-approved so that organisers need not seek the same venue-level permissions for each event.

The LEDC further reviewed the framework for “Brownfield and Greenfield Venue Development” to address the shortage of purpose-built venues. State Governments, industry stakeholders and sports authorities were requested to provide their formal feedback on the draft framework. Proposals discussed include identification and development of purpose-built venues by States, inclusion of live event and performance venues above a threshold capacity in the Harmonised Master List of Infrastructure Sub-sectors, and project support through the Viability Gap Funding scheme.

The Live Event Skilling Committee, chaired by the Vice Chancellor, Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC), presented the progress on the skilling curriculum, including the MoU between IIMC, MESC and EEMA, and certificate and short-term courses in live events. Stakeholders were encouraged to adopt these modules through their skilling institutions. It was also proposed that Inclusivity Guidelines for Safety of Women and Divyang-jan at Live Events and Concerts and a Green Concert Protocol be launched at WAVES 2027 with the support of the industry.

The meeting concluded with the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting reaffirming its commitment to working closely with all stakeholders to foster a supportive and growth-oriented ecosystem for India's live events sector.

*****

Mahesh Kumar/ Aparajita Priyadarshini

The exercise will witness the participation and observation of 32 delegates from 30 foreign friendly nations. Addressing the gathering, RRM welcomed the representatives of international organisations and friendly foreign countries and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
RRM Inaugurates SAREX-2026 as 24th NMSAR Board Meeting Reviews Maritime SAR Preparedness
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth inaugurated the Multinational Search and Rescue Exercise (SAREX-2026) on October 07, 2026, set to be conducted off Paradip on October 08, 2026. The exercise will witness the participation and observation of 32 delegates from 30 foreign friendly nations.

Addressing the gathering, RRM welcomed the representatives of international organisations and friendly foreign countries and appreciated their presence as the mutual commitment towards enhancing cooperation and strengthening maritime safety across the region. He said the participation of the Navy, Coast Guard, Air Force, Coastal Police, Ports, Civil Agencies, Shipping Community and international and regional partners demonstrates that modern maritime security is not the responsibility of any single agency, but requires a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Nation approach.

The Raksha Rajya Mantri highlighted India's continued efforts to strengthen its Search and Rescue capabilities through cooperation, preparedness and technological advancement. He noted that India's journey in Satellite Aided Search and Rescue has progressively evolved from Low Earth Orbit Search and Rescue (LEOSAR) to Geostationary Search and Rescue (GEOSAR) and now towards Medium Earth Orbit Search and Rescue (MEOSAR). He described the achievement of full operations capability of the Indian Earth Orbit Local User Terminal (MEOLUT) as a significant advancement in India's satellite-aided Search and Rescue capability. RRM congratulated ISRO and all associated teams for the achievement and their contribution towards strengthening India's national Search and Rescue (SAR) capabilities.

The Raksha Rajya Mantri called upon all participating agencies and international partners to reaffirm their shared commitment to safeguarding lives at sea and to strengthen the spirit of cooperation that underpins effective Search and Rescue across the region. Invoking the principle of ‘One Earth, One Family, One Future’, he said collective efforts can build a safer, more resilient and more cooperative maritime community.

Shri Seth emphasised that as India moves towards the aspirations of Viksit Bharat 2047, its SAR capabilities must evolve, becoming faster, accurate and more resilient. He said a developed and empowered India must also become a safe, resilient and technologically advanced maritime nation, as reflected meaningfully in the motto of the Indian Coast Guard - Vayam Rakshamah (We Protect).”

SAREX-2026 is a multi-agency exercise aimed at validating operational preparedness, enhancing international interoperability, testing joint response mechanisms and fostering the exchange of best practices, with preservation of life at sea as the paramount objective of every mission.

The 24th National Maritime Search and Rescue (NMSAR) Board Meeting was also convened earlier today under the chairmanship of Director General Paramesh Sivamani, DG Indian Coast Guard and Chairman, NMSAR Board on October 07, 2026. The board reviewed the preparedness of maritime Search and Rescue operations across the 4.6 million sq km Indian Search & Rescue Region (ISRR). During the meeting, deliberations were held on technological integration, real-time information sharing, distress-alert management, vessel tracking and inter-agency coordination, providing the operational foundation for SAREX-2026.     The Chairman underscored that operational lessons derived from past missions and multi-agency exercises must directly translate into heightened mission readiness and response capabilities.The meeting also witnessed the presentation of the National Maritime Search & Rescue Awards 2026, recognising exemplary efforts in saving lives at sea.

**********

SR/Ruchi

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
NLMC Organises Mock E-Auction Training Ahead of RINL Land E-Auction
459 RINL Land Parcels Covering 93,572.21 Sq. Yards to be Auctioned on October 12 and 16
Registration and EMD Submission for First Auction Open Till October 8, 2026, 5:00 PM
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi

The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC), under the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, conducted a physical mock e-auction platform training in Visakhapatnam on October 6, 2026, to familiarise prospective bidders with the online bidding process ahead of the upcoming e-auction of 459 land parcels of Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), the corporate entity of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant.

The hands-on training was organised for providing prospective bidders and other interested stakeholders an opportunity to experience the e-auction platform in a simulated environment. The sessions covered the bidding interface, participation procedure and other key aspects of the online auction process, enabling participants to gain practical familiarity with the platform ahead of the live auctions.

To facilitate participation by prospective bidders who could not attend the physical training, NLMC also conducted an online mock e-auction platform training on October 7, 2026. The online session provided participants an opportunity to familiarise themselves with the digital bidding process remotely ahead of the live auctions scheduled for October 12 and 16, 2026.

The mock e-auction initiatives are being conducted just days ahead of the two-phase RINL land e-auction, with the first phase scheduled for October 12, 2026, from 11:00 AM to 7:00 PM, followed by the second phase on October 16, 2026, from 11:00 AM to 7:00 PM.

During the event, CEO, NLMC, Shri Rohan Chand Thakur said that, the physical and online mock e-auction sessions are important steps towards ensuring that prospective bidders are familiar with the digital bidding process ahead of the live auctions. Our endeavour is to make the auction process transparent, accessible and participant-friendly, while providing prospective bidders adequate opportunity to understand the platform and complete the necessary formalities within the prescribed timelines. The RINL land auction presents a significant asset monetisation opportunity, and NLMC remains committed to facilitating the process in a professional, transparent and structured manner.

459 Land Parcels Spread Across 93,572.21 Square Yards

The RINL land portfolio comprises 459 premium, encumbrance-free plots aggregating 93,572.21 square yards in Visakhapatnam, including locations such as HB Colony, Maddilapalem and Auto Nagar, Gajuwaka.

  

The plots range in size from approximately 128.94 square yards to 2,728 square yards, offering prospective buyers a range of options across the identified locations.

The properties are being offered through a transparent and competitive e-tender-cum-e-auction process on the RailTel E-Nivida e-Procurement Platform. Quikr India Pvt. Ltd. (QIPL) is the Transaction Consultant for the process.

Important Auction Dates

Prospective bidders interested in the first phase of the auction on October 12 are required to complete the registration process, fulfil the prescribed requirements and submit the EMD by October 8, 2026, up to 5:00 PM.

For the second phase scheduled on October 16, the last date for registration and EMD submission is October 14, 2026, up to 5:00 PM.

   

Investor Outreach Across Three Cities

Ahead of the auction, NLMC also conducted Investor Meets in Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Hyderabad, providing prospective buyers and other stakeholders an opportunity to obtain detailed information about the land parcels, auction process, eligibility requirements and related procedures.

The Investor Meets witnessed participation from prospective buyers through both physical and virtual modes, including participants based outside the region and overseas. The physical and online mock e-auction sessions further strengthen this outreach by providing prospective bidders with practical exposure to the digital bidding platform.

The two-pronged mock training initiative, physical training in Visakhapatnam on October 6 and online training on October 7, is aimed at ensuring wider access and greater bidder preparedness before the live auctions.

NLMC is facilitating the monetisation of surplus land and non-core assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and Government agencies as part of the Government’s broader objective of unlocking the value of under-utilised assets through transparent and structured processes.

Prospective bidders can access detailed information regarding the RINL land e-auction, including plot details, auction schedule, eligibility criteria, terms and conditions, registration requirements and bidding process, on the official e-auction portal:

E-Auction Portal: https://eauction.enivida.com/

About NLMC

The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC) is a Government of India-owned company under the administrative control of the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance. NLMC facilitates the monetisation of surplus land and non-core assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises and other Government agencies through a structured and professional framework.

About RINL

Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), the corporate entity of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, is a Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Steel, Government of India.

item.title: From Financial Constraints to Scientific Achievement: Balamurugan S.’s Journey through National Fellowship Support
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment From Financial Constraints to Scientific Achievement: Balamurugan S.’s Journey through National Fellowship Support Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi Financial assistance for higher education and research can play an important role in enabling students from disadvantaged communities to pursue advanced studies, overcome economic barriers and contribute to scientific advancement. Timely fellowship support can provide students with the financial stability required to focus on research and achieve their academic…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Constraints to Scientific Achievement: Balamurugan S.’s Journey through National Fellowship Support
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi

Financial assistance for higher education and research can play an important role in enabling students from disadvantaged communities to pursue advanced studies, overcome economic barriers and contribute to scientific advancement. Timely fellowship support can provide students with the financial stability required to focus on research and achieve their academic aspirations.

Shri Balamurugan S., aged 35, belongs to the Devendra Kula Velalar community and is a Scheduled Caste beneficiary. Currently working as a Guest Lecturer of Physics, he is the first graduate in his family and the only person in his family lineage to have received a doctoral degree. While higher education was an attainable goal for him, financial constraints posed a significant challenge in pursuing advanced studies and scientific research.

Receiving support under the National Fellowship provided Shri Balamurugan with the financial assistance needed to dedicate himself fully to his research. During the fellowship period from 2017 to 2020, he received financial support of Rs. 25,000 per month during the first two years and Rs. 31,000 per month during the subsequent two years. The fellowship proved to be an important source of support in conducting specialised research involving chemicals and advanced techniques such as X-Ray Diffraction (XRD), X-Ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), antimicrobial studies and magnetic studies.

With the support of the fellowship, Shri Balamurugan successfully completed his research and pursued his aspiration of making an original contribution to the scientific community. He authored and published a research paper on “Cadmium Oxide Nanopowders,” which he describes as the world's first research paper on the subject. The fellowship support also contributed to his continued research work and enabled him to publish 28 international research papers.

The National Fellowship has significantly contributed to Shri Balamurugan's academic and research journey, enabling him to overcome financial limitations and pursue higher education with greater focus and confidence. His achievement as the only person in his family lineage to attain a doctoral degree has also marked an important milestone for his family.

Shri Balamurugan says, “Receiving the National Fellowship provided me with the support I needed to dedicate myself fully to scientific research. It helped me complete my research and publish 28 international research papers.”

Shri Balamurugan S.’s journey demonstrates how financial assistance for higher education and research can enable talented students from disadvantaged communities to pursue advanced studies, undertake scientific research and contribute to the wider academic community. His experience reflects the role of fellowship support in creating opportunities for higher learning, scientific advancement and greater self-reliance.

SS-118-TAR-KV-GA-RK

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
ICAR Reviews Development and Digitisation of Domain-Specific iGOT Courses
Dr. M. L. Jat directs ICAR Institutes to ensure quality, timely completion and regular learning on iGOT Karmayogi platform
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi

The Agricultural Education Division of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) today organised an online review meeting to assess the development and digitisation of domain-specific courses for the iGOT Karmayogi platform. The meeting was chaired by Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, ICAR.

The meeting was organised to review the progress of domain-specific course development by ICAR Institutes and to ensure their timely uploading on the iGOT Karmayogi platform in accordance with prescribed guidelines.

Addressing the meeting, Dr. M. L. Jat directed all ICAR Institutes to develop and upload high-quality domain-specific courses after undertaking proper internal review and ensuring adherence to the prescribed guidelines. He emphasised the importance of completing the assigned work within the stipulated timelines and strengthening regular learning through the iGOT Karmayogi platform.

Dr. Jat also emphasised that all ICAR employees should undertake at least two hours of learning regularly on the iGOT Karmayogi platform. He called upon all ICAR Institutes to ensure active participation and timely completion of the assigned learning hours and course-uploading targets.

In his opening remarks, Dr. Yashpal Singh Malik, Deputy Director General (Agricultural Education), ICAR, highlighted the need for timely action by all ICAR Institutes to strengthen ICAR's performance under Mission Karmayogi. He stressed the importance of active participation of all Institutes in improving ICAR's national-level ranking under the Mission Karmayogi framework.

During the meeting, Mr. Ashwin, Expert from Karmayogi Bharat, briefed the participants on the process of content development and digitisation of courses. He also provided information on empanelled agencies available for course development and shared technical inputs to facilitate the creation and uploading of quality domain-specific learning content.

The meeting concluded with directions for expediting course development and digitisation, ensuring quality through internal review, completing assigned learning hours and uploading domain-specific courses within the stipulated timelines. Active participation of all ICAR Institutes was emphasised for strengthening capacity building and learning under Mission Karmayogi.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Financial Support Today, Self-Reliance Tomorrow
Manikala Durga’s Journey towards Economic Self-Reliance
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi

Timely support for livelihood activities can provide opportunities to enhance income, strengthen family financial security and promote greater dignity and self-reliance. Financial assistance can play an important role in helping individuals from disadvantaged communities establish sustainable livelihoods and improve their economic condition.

Ms. Manikala Durga, aged 39, belongs to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) community and has been working as a waste picker in the Guntur Municipal Corporation for the past 15 years. Coming from a financially disadvantaged family, she could not attend school and remained illiterate. Before receiving assistance, her livelihood depended primarily on waste-picking activities, through which she earned approximately Rs. 8,000 per month. Her limited income made it difficult to meet household expenses and provide better opportunities for her children.

Ms. Durga, along with three other members, received financial assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) of the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation through Navajeevan Organisation. The assistance was provided in the form of an upfront capital subsidy for procurement of a De-Silting Machine for Open Drain Cleaning (Excavator with Backhoe Bucket). The group project had a total project cost of Rs. 35,03,500, comprising a loan of Rs. 21,27,624 and a capital subsidy of Rs. 13,75,876. The support was provided on 19 June 2023.

With the effective utilisation of the financial assistance, Ms. Durga has been able to generate an additional income of approximately Rs. 8,000 per month, taking her total monthly income to around Rs. 16,000. The increase in income has strengthened her ability to meet household needs and support her family in a more stable and secure manner.

The assistance under the SUY scheme has significantly improved Ms. Durga’s economic condition and provided her with an opportunity to pursue a more sustainable livelihood. The increased earning capacity has enhanced her financial security and confidence, while enabling her to contribute more effectively towards the well-being of her family and the education and future of her children.

Ms Durga expressed her contentment and said, ““The financial assistance has helped me increase my income and improve my family’s financial condition. It has given me greater confidence, financial stability and an opportunity to work towards a better future for my children.”

Ms. Manikala Durga’s journey demonstrates how timely financial assistance and livelihood support can enable individuals from disadvantaged communities to improve their earning capacity and move towards economic self-reliance. Her experience reflects the role of targeted financial support in creating sustainable livelihood opportunities, strengthening families and promoting a more dignified and self-reliant society.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
ICAR Reviews Progress of Nine Committees on Action Points of 5th National Conference of Chief Secretaries
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) today reviewed the progress of nine committees constituted to address key action points emerging from the 5th National Conference of Chief Secretaries, held in December 2025. The review meeting was chaired by Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, ICAR.

The committees are working on 28 action points aimed at strengthening human capital for Viksit Bharat, with a focus on higher education, skills, innovation and capacity building. The review was undertaken to assess the progress made by the committees and facilitate timely formulation of actionable recommendations.

Addressing the meeting, Dr. M. L. Jat emphasised the need for evidence-based, measurable and implementable recommendations to strengthen human capital and higher education towards Viksit Bharat. He stressed that the recommendations should be supported by relevant data, documented evidence and best practices, enabling effective implementation and measurable outcomes.

In his opening remarks, Dr. Yashpal Singh Malik, Deputy Director General (Agricultural Education), ICAR, highlighted the importance of coordinated efforts by the committees for addressing the identified action points within the stipulated timelines. He underscored the need for a structured approach to translating the deliberations of the National Conference of Chief Secretaries into concrete and implementable outcomes.

During the meeting, the Member Secretaries of the nine committees presented the progress made on their respective action points. The presentations covered key achievements, progress against identified areas, existing gaps and proposed recommendations. The discussions also focused on strengthening the recommendations through relevant data, evidence and best practices.

The review provided an opportunity to assess the progress of the committees, identify areas requiring further attention and facilitate convergence among the ongoing efforts towards strengthening higher education, skills, innovation and capacity building.

The meeting concluded with an emphasis on timely submission of evidence-based, measurable and implementable recommendations by the committees for further consideration and action.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
From 4,000-Year-Old Dhokra to Tribal Heritage, Chhattisgarh’s Cultural Story Comes Alive at the 8th PM Mementos
Collection showcases Chhattisgarh’s ancient metal-casting traditions, tribal heritage, devotional art and contemporary cultural identity
You can bid for these mementos through the official PM Mementos portal
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 5:39PM by PIB Delhi

An ancient metal-casting tradition takes centre stage in a collection of 16 mementos from Chhattisgarh, bringing together the state’s rich tribal heritage, devotional traditions and contemporary cultural identity.

 

 

At the heart of the collection is Dhokra, the traditional lost-wax metal-casting craft having a history of more than 4,000 years in India. Several Dhokra works showcase the distinctive character and versatility of the tradition, including an Elephant Head Nandi, Standing Nandi and Madia-Madin Tribal Couple Bust.

The story of tribal Chhattisgarh continues through a traditional ceremonial headgear featuring a peacock-feather cluster, cowrie shells, metallic discs and brass bells.

Beyond tribal craft, the collection brings together the many cultural influences that shape the state. A Ramnami Samaj chanting stole, covered with repeated inscriptions of “Ram Ram”, represents a distinctive expression of faith and devotion. Other mementos depict important religious and cultural landmarks, including Hatkeshwar Mahadev, Budeshwar Mahadev, Jai Maa Kudargadi and Madheshwar Mahadev.

 

 

The collection also captures a more contemporary Chhattisgarh. A woodcut panel depicting the Mahtari Vandan Yojana, a memento marking the Rajat Jayanti of the Chhattisgarh Vidhan Sabha, and models representing institutions in Nava Raipur reflect the state’s evolving present alongside its traditional heritage.

The collection’s central message is one of continuity. Traditions that have been shaped over generations continue to find expression in contemporary objects, carrying the cultural memory of Chhattisgarh forward.

The auction is currently live and has been extended until 31 October 2026. Proceeds from the auction will support the Namami Gange Project.

Interested bidders can place their bids online through the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal: https://pmmementos.gov.in .

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Communications
item.description: Ministry of Communications Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Leads Interaction with Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) Board Members alongside Union Minister for Communications Jyotiraditya Scindia and Minister of State Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani Technology must become a tool for inclusive and sustainable development: Prime Minister Technology-driven solutions needed to tackle cyber fraud: Prime Minister GSMA Board Members applaud India’s digital transformation and growing global technology partnerships Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 5:23PM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Leads Interaction with Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) Board Members alongside Union Minister for Communications Jyotiraditya Scindia and Minister of State Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani
Technology must become a tool for inclusive and sustainable development: Prime Minister
Technology-driven solutions needed to tackle cyber fraud: Prime Minister
GSMA Board Members applaud India’s digital transformation and growing global technology partnerships
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 5:23PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacted with Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) Board members at Seva Teerth ahead of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026. GSMA is a global organisation unifying the mobile ecosystem, representing mobile operators and organisations across the mobile ecosystem and adjacent industries.

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia attended the interaction along with Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development Dr. Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar and senior officials of the Government of India.

Prime Minister emphasised that technology must become a tool for inclusive and sustainable development. He stressed that democratisation of technology is essential to ensure that no section of society is left behind. He underlined the need to make technology and digital services affordable and accessible, particularly for the Global South, and highlighted the importance of taking technology to the last mile to prevent a widening digital divide.

Prime Minister highlighted the potential of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) as a transformative force, particularly for developing countries. He noted that discussions on DPI with several world leaders had demonstrated its growing global relevance and said that such platforms can serve as a springboard for countries of the Global South.

Addressing the growing challenge of digital and cyber fraud, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi said the problem requires technology-driven solutions. He suggested sustained awareness messages for users to warn people about potential fraud calls.

Prime Minister also highlighted the need for global standards and common rules for emerging technologies. On the growing threat of deepfakes and AI-generated content, he suggested exploring mechanisms to allow users to immediately identify its origin.

GSMA Board members recognise India’s digital transformation

GSMA Board members highlighted India’s emergence as a global leader in digital and mobile connectivity. They noted the rapid expansion of 4G and 5G, the scale of Digital Public Infrastructure and the growth of India’s telecom and mobile manufacturing ecosystem.

They appreciated India’s investment-friendly policy framework and emphasised the role of secure, resilient and trusted digital infrastructure in supporting continued digital growth.

The Board members also highlighted growing opportunities for international cooperation with India in areas including 5G, 6G, AI, cybersecurity, digital inclusion and satellite connectivity.

Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia’s global telecom engagement strengthens India’s technology partnerships

The interaction comes as India prepares to host the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress, bringing together global technology and telecom leaders in New Delhi.

Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia has been leading India’s international engagement on next-generation connectivity and digital technologies. At Mobile World Congress 2026 in Barcelona, he led India’s engagements with the global telecom ecosystem and addressed the GSMA Ministerial Programme on making connectivity more affordable, inclusive and future-ready.

India’s engagement with global technology leaders reflects the country’s growing role in shaping the future of telecommunications, including the evolution of 6G, secure digital infrastructure, Artificial Intelligence and globally interoperable technology standards.

With India increasingly contributing to global conversations on next-generation connectivity and digital public infrastructure, the interaction with the GSMA Board further strengthens India’s partnerships with the global mobile ecosystem.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance
item.description: Ministry of Finance Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) conducts Jan Samvad at Malana in Kullu District to create preventive drug awareness and to promote development Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 5:19PM by PIB Delhi The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India, organised a Jan Samvad at Malana village in Kullu district, Himachal Pradesh, on October 6, 2026, as part of its Preventive Outreach under Yuva Raksha initiatives and efforts towards fulfilling CBN’s mandate to promoting alternative development in illicit…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) conducts Jan Samvad at Malana in Kullu District to create preventive drug awareness and to promote development
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 5:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India, organised a Jan Samvad at Malana village in Kullu district, Himachal Pradesh, on October 6, 2026, as part of its Preventive Outreach under Yuva Raksha initiatives and efforts towards fulfilling CBN’s mandate to promoting alternative development in illicit cannabis cultivation affected areas as per India's National Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) policy, 2012 and Vision document on Narcotics Control 2026–2029.

The initiative is in furtherance of the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for a Nasha Mukt Bharat (Drug-Free India) and seeks to contribute to the objectives of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan through sustained preventive awareness, youth engagement and community participation.

 

Officers of the Central Bureau of Narcotics and people of Malana village discussing during Jan samvad at Malana village

Malana village is known for its distinctive cultural heritage, traditional community institutions and its long-standing association with illicit cannabis grown areas. "As part of its Jan Samvad initiative, the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) conducted awareness drives to sensitize rural youth and populations on the harmful impacts of cannabis (ganja), charas, and hashish oil consumption. Concurrently, the CBN actively encouraged villagers to adopt alternative development and cropping systems and sustainable livelihood models supported by the various departments."

The discussions also focused on challenges faced by the community in developing alternative livelihoods, including difficulties in Apple cultivation, connectivity, market linkages and fair prices for agricultural produce. Opportunities in apiculture, animal husbandry and dairy-related activities, tourism and other locally suitable livelihood avenues were also discussed. The impact of illicit cannabis cultivation on local ecology, including reduction in grazing areas traditionally available for sheep and goats and concerns relating to deforestation, was also discussed.

The interaction was constructive and provided an opportunity for the CBN team and the local community to discuss practical challenges as well as possible avenues for sustainable development and alternative livelihood generation.

 

 Malana villages taking collective pledge to refrain from drug consumption and to discontinue illicit cannabis cultivation

At the conclusion of the Jan Samvad, community members took a collective pledge to refrain from drug consumption and to discourage illicit cannabis cultivation in the coming cultivation season, while working with CBN to explore alternative livelihood and crop-development opportunities. School children also took a pledge to remain drug-free and contribute towards building a healthy and drug-free community.

School children of Malana village taking pledge to remain drug free.

The Jan Samvad reflects CBN’s continued emphasis on combining enforcement with preventive awareness, community participation and promotion of sustainable alternatives to illicit cultivation.

item.content:encoded:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAYS TRIBUTES TO FORMER SPEAKER, LOK SABHA, SHRI BALI RAM BHAGAT
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 5:05PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi; 7 October, 2026: Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla paid floral tributes to former Speaker, Lok Sabha, Shri Bali Ram Bhagat, at his portrait in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan on his Birth Anniversary, today.

Secretary-General, Lok Sabha, Shri Utpal Kumar Singh also paid tributes to Shri Bhagat.

A veteran freedom fighter with rich parliamentary experience and deep knowledge of parliamentary practices and procedures, Shri Bhagat was elected as the Speaker of the Fifth Lok Sabha on 5 January 1976. He was a Member of the Provisional Parliament and First, Second, Third, Fourth, Fifth, Seventh and Eighth Lok Sabhas.

As a Union Minister, he held important portfolios, including Finance, Planning, Defence, External Affairs, Foreign Trade and Supply, Steel and Heavy

Engineering. He functioned as the Governor of Himachal Pradesh from February

1993 for four months and Governor of Rajasthan from 30 June 1993 till 1 May 1998.

Shri Bali Ram Bhagat passed away in New Delhi on 2 January 2011.

लोक सभा के पूर्व अध्यक्ष एवं राजस्थान के राज्यपाल रहे स्व. श्री बलि राम भगत जी की जयंती पर संविधान सदन के केंद्रीय कक्ष में भावपूर्ण श्रद्धासुमन अर्पित किए। श्री बलि राम भगत का सार्वजनिक जीवन स्वतंत्रता संग्राम, संसदीय लोकतंत्र, प्रशासन और सामाजिक सरोकार की एक लंबी एवं बहुआयामी यात्रा रहा। करीब चार दशकों के विधायी जीवन के साथ श्री बलि राम भगत ने संसदीय लोकतंत्र को मजबूत करने में उल्लेखनीय भूमिका निभाई। वर्ष 1950 में वे Provisional Parliament के लिए निर्वाचित हुए। इसके बाद पहली से पाँचवीं लोक सभा तक 1952 से 1977 के बीच और फिर सातवीं तथा आठवीं लोक सभा में 1980 से 1989 तक संसद के सदस्य रहे। उन्होंने सात बार लोक सभा का प्रतिनिधित्व किया। 5 जनवरी 1976 को श्री बलि राम भगत पाँचवीं लोक सभा के अध्यक्ष निर्वाचित हुए। यह उनके संसदीय जीवन का एक महत्वपूर्ण पड़ाव था। अध्यक्ष पद संभालते समय उन्होंने स्पष्ट रूप से कहा कि Speaker सदन का servant होता है और सदन के सभी वर्गों से समान रूप से संबंधित होता है। उन्होंने अपने दायित्वों को impartiality और निष्पक्षता के साथ निभाने की प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त की। उनकी अध्यक्षीय कार्यशैली में संसदीय प्रक्रियाओं की गहरी समझ, संयम और व्यवस्था के प्रति दृढ़ प्रतिबद्धता दिखाई दी। उनकी parliamentary skill, procedural knowledge, insight तथा holistic vision के कारण सदन के विभिन्न वर्गों में उनके प्रति सम्मान था। श्री भगत संसदीय अनुशासन और सदन की मर्यादा को लेकर अत्यंत सजग थे। वे Parliamentary traditions और propriety के दृढ़ समर्थक थे। वे मानते थे कि संसदीय कार्यवाही प्रभावी तभी हो सकती है जब नियमों, समय और प्रक्रियाओं का सम्मान किया जाए। उनकी अध्यक्षीय कार्यशैली में यह विशेष रूप से दिखाई देता था कि कठिन परिस्थितियों में भी वे शांत और संयमित रहते हुए सदन के नियमों का पालन सुनिश्चित करने का प्रयास करते थे। श्री बलि राम भगत की संसदीय विरासत का एक महत्वपूर्ण पहलू उनकी institution-building approach थी। मार्च 1976 में उनके अध्यक्षीय कार्यकाल के दौरान Committee of Chairmen on Government Assurances का पहला सम्मेलन आयोजित हुआ। उन्होंने इस बात पर जोर दिया कि सदन के पटल पर सरकार द्वारा दिए गए आश्वासनों का उचित रूप से पालन और कार्यान्वयन सुनिश्चित होना चाहिए। इसी वर्ष Parliamentary Research and Training Institute for Democracies/PRIDE (Erstwhile BPST) की स्थापना हुई, जो आज लोक सभा सचिवालय का एक महत्वपूर्ण अंग है। संसदीय अध्ययन और प्रशिक्षण की यह पहल जनप्रतिनिधियों तथा संसदीय कार्य से जुड़े लोगों के लिए क्षमता निर्माण की दिशा में महत्वपूर्ण कदम थी। यह उनकी उस सोच को दर्शाता है जिसमें संसद को केवल बहस और कानून निर्माण का मंच नहीं, बल्कि ज्ञान, प्रशिक्षण, प्रक्रियागत दक्षता और संस्थागत क्षमता से मजबूत होने वाली लोकतांत्रिक संस्था के रूप में देखा गया। श्री बलि राम भगत जी का जीवन स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन से शुरू होकर स्वतंत्र भारत की लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं के विकास के लिए समर्पित रहा। वे राजस्थान और हिमाचल प्रदेश के राज्यपाल तथा केंद्रीय विदेश मंत्री के पद पर भी रहे। उन्होंने स्वतंत्रता के लिए संघर्ष किया, संसद में जनता का प्रतिनिधित्व किया, केंद्र सरकार में विदेश मंत्री के रूप में महत्वपूर्ण ज़िम्मेदारी निभाईं तथा लोक सभा अध्यक्ष के रूप में संसदीय मर्यादा और प्रक्रियाओं को महत्व दिया। श्री बलि राम भगत जी की संसदीय विरासत, लोकतांत्रिक प्रतिबद्धता, सामाजिक सरोकार और राष्ट्रसेवा की भावना आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए सदैव प्रेरणा का स्रोत बनी रहेगी।

Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri approves Revised Standard Operating Procedure for Utilisation of MoD Proof Ranges, Field Firing Ranges & Test Facilities by Indian Defence Industry
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 4:58PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has approved revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Utilisation of MoD Proof Ranges, Field Firing Ranges & Test Facilities by Indian Defence Industry. The revised SOP provides for a detailed and simplified procedure for allotment and utilisation of MoD proof ranges and laboratory testing facilities, along with requisite formats.

The key features of the revised SOP are as follows:

  • Proof/testing charges have been waived for iDEX, TDF, Make and other developmental projects of the Ministry of Defence, to promote ‘Atmanirbharta in Defence’.
  • The SOP lists the Proof Ranges, Field Firing Ranges and Laboratory Test Facilities available with DRDO, Government Quality Assurance agencies and the three Services for utilisation by the Indian defence industry.
  • The procedure for calculation and payment of proof/testing charges, wherever applicable, has been incorporated in the SOP, thereby simplifying the documentation and process for industry.
  • The provision for Arbitration in the existing SOP has been replaced with a simpler and industry-friendly Conciliation Agreement Clause, to facilitate Ease of Doing Business through faster resolution of issues faced by the indigenous defence industry.
  • A three-day slot per quarter has been reserved at Proof Ranges for proof firing of developmental projects sponsored by the Government, including iDEX, TDF, Make and other developmental projects of the Ministry of Defence, as well as developmental projects undertaken under the own initiative of the indigenous defence industry.

The revised SOP aims to provide simpler, transparent and industry-friendly access to proof ranges, field firing ranges and test facilities. It incorporates various Government initiatives aimed at facilitating indigenisation, innovation and defence exports, besides providing proof and test support to developmental projects undertaken by the Indian defence industry.

******

SR/Sumitra

Prime Minister's Office
World leaders congratulate Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on completion of 25 years as Head of Government
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 4:56PM by PIB Delhi

World leaders from across continents have extended their warmest greetings and hearty congratulations to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on completing a historic milestone of 25 continuous years as Head of Government on October 7, 2026. Marking twenty five years since he first assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat in 2001 and subsequently taking over as the Prime Minister of the Republic of India in 2014, global leaders highlighted his transformative leadership, dedication to good governance, and commitment to global peace, inclusivity, and sustainable development.

Prime Minister of Bhutan, H.E. Tshering Tobgay, congratulated the Prime Minister on this historic milestone. Sharing a letter, he noted that enlightened leadership is the exercise of wisdom, compassion, and courage through selfless service, qualities he sees coming together most clearly in PM Modi's vision of Viksit Bharat. Emphasizing that this vision reflects the collective ambition of 1.4 billion Indians for a strong, prosperous, and developed country, he posted on X;

"To Prime Minister @narendramodi, An avatar of our times

To Prime Minister @narendramodi, An avatar of our times https://t.co/84RDOEfELm

— Tshering Tobgay (@tsheringtobgay) October 7, 2026

President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, H.E. Bola Ahmed Tinubu, extended warm and fraternal congratulations to PM Modi. Highlighting the visionary leadership that steered the transformation of Gujarat and facilitated India's rise as one of the fastest growing global economies, he shared on X;

"On behalf of the Government and people of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and on my own behalf, I extend warm and fraternal congratulations to His Excellency Shri Narendra Modi @narendramodi, Prime Minister of the Republic of India, on a truly historic milestone. 

Today, 7 October 2026, marks 25 years since he first assumed office in 2001 as Head of Government and Chief Minister of Gujarat.

His public service has continued without interruption. After more than twelve years serving the people of Gujarat, he has remained Prime Minister of the Republic of India since 2014. 

A quarter-century of unbroken leadership is a rare achievement in any democracy. In the world's most populous nation, it is a powerful testament to the enduring confidence the Indian people have placed in him.

Across these 25 years, Prime Minister Modi has led with vision and an unwavering commitment to development. From the transformation of Gujarat to India's emergence as one of the world's largest and fastest-growing economies, his leadership in infrastructure, digital public goods, financial inclusion and innovation has lifted millions and inspired nations across the Global South.

Nigeria deeply values the strategic partnership between our two great nations. I fondly recall the Prime Minister's historic State Visit to Abuja in November 2024, when Nigeria honoured him with the title of Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger. 

That visit gave fresh impetus to our cooperation in trade and investment, energy, defence and security, health, education, and technology.

As fellow democracies and leading voices of the Global South, Nigeria and India share a common commitment to a fairer, more inclusive and more representative international order. I remain confident that, under his continued leadership, the bonds of friendship between our peoples will grow ever stronger.

As Prime Minister Modi marks this remarkable anniversary, I wish him good health, continued strength and every success in the service of the people of India.

Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR

President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces

Federal Republic of Nigeria

Abuja, 7 October 2026"

— Bart De Wever (@Bart_DeWever) October 7, 2026

Prime Minister of Japan, H.E. Sanae Takaichi, expressed her heartfelt greetings to PM Modi on completing this 25 year milestone. Highlighting his excellent political leadership that has accelerated India's development and raised its international prestige to new heights, and looking forward to working together to realize a Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP), she posted on X;

"प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के सरकार के प्रमुख के तौर पर 25 वर्ष की अवधि पूरे होने पर मैं अपनी शुभकामनाएँ व्यक्त करना चाहती हूँ।

भारत के समाज और राष्ट्र के विकास को साकार करने के लिए वे वर्षों से प्रयास करते आए हैं और सन् 2001 से अपने उत्कृष्ट राजनीतिक नेतृत्व से सरकार के प्रमुख के पद संभालते आए हैं। उन्होंने भारत के विकास को गति देने के साथ ही अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर पर भी भारत की प्रतिष्ठा को नई ऊंचाइयों तक पहुंचाया। इन सारी उपलब्धियों के लिए, मैं एक साथी राजनीतिज्ञ के रूप में सम्मान भावना व्यक्त करती हूँ।

मैं फिर से प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी का आभार व्यक्त करना चाहती हूँ कि इस जुलाई में मेरी भारत यात्रा के दौरान मुझे उनका बेहद गर्मजोशी भरा स्वागत मिला।

भारत की खाद्य संस्कृति और संगीत का अनुभव करते हुए, मुझे जापान-भारत की "विशेष रणनीतिक और वैश्विक साझेदारी" को अगले स्तर तक ले जाने के लिए उनके साथ ठोस कदमों पर विचार-विमर्श करने का शुभ अवसर प्राप्त हुआ। मेरी भारत यात्रा बहुत ही फलदायी रही।

अगले वर्ष जापान-भारत राजनयिक संबंधों की स्थापना की 75वीं वर्षगाँठ है।

मुक्त एवं खुले हिन्द-प्रशांत क्षेत्र (FOIP) को साकार करने हेतु मैं प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के साथ मिलकर काम करना चाहती हूँ ताकि रणनीतिक दिशा को साझा करने वाले जापान तथा भारत मिलकर हमारी साझेदारी को और आगे बढ़ाया जा सके।"

 

本日、モディ首相（@narendramodi）の首長在職25周年に際し、心からお祝い申し上げます。 インドの社会と国家の発展に長年尽力され、2001年以降は首長として長きにわたり卓越した政治的リーダーシップを発揮されてきたこと、インドの発展と国際社会における地位向上を成し遂げられていることに、深い敬意を表します。 また、本年7月の私のインド訪問の際には、大変温かいおもてなしをいただき、改めて感謝申し上げます。 インドの食文化や音楽に触れながら、日印の「特別戦略的グローバル・パートナーシップ」を新たな段階へと導くための施策について、モディ首相と具体的な意見交換を行うことができ、実り多き滞在となりました。 来年は「日印国交樹立75周年」を迎えます。 「自由で開かれたインド太平洋（FOIP）」の実現のため、戦略的方向性を共有する日印で、パートナーシップを更に前に進めるべく、モディ首相と一層連携していきます。 प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के सरकार के प्रमुख के तौर पर 25 वर्ष की अवधि पूरे होने पर मैं अपनी शुभकामनाएँ व्यक्त करना चाहती हूँ। भारत के समाज और राष्ट्र के विकास को साकार करने के लिए वे वर्षों से प्रयास करते आए हैं और सन् 2001 से अपने उत्कृष्ट राजनीतिक नेतृत्व से सरकार के प्रमुख के पद संभालते आए हैं। उन्होंने भारत के विकास को गति देने के साथ ही अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर पर भी भारत की प्रतिष्ठा को नई ऊंचाइयों तक पहुंचाया। इन सारी उपलब्धियों के लिए, मैं एक साथी राजनीतिज्ञ के रूप में सम्मान भावना व्यक्त करती हूँ। मैं फिर से प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी का आभार व्यक्त करना चाहती हूँ कि इस जुलाई में मेरी भारत यात्रा के दौरान मुझे उनका बेहद गर्मजोशी भरा स्वागत मिला। भारत की खाद्य संस्कृति और संगीत का अनुभव करते हुए, मुझे जापान-भारत की "विशेष रणनीतिक और वैश्विक साझेदारी" को अगले स्तर तक ले जाने के लिए उनके साथ ठोस कदमों पर विचार-विमर्श करने का शुभ अवसर प्राप्त हुआ। मेरी भारत यात्रा बहुत ही फलदायी रही। अगले वर्ष जापान-भारत राजनयिक संबंधों की स्थापना की 75वीं वर्षगाँठ है। मुक्त एवं खुले हिन्द-प्रशांत क्षेत्र (FOIP) को साकार करने हेतु मैं प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के साथ मिलकर काम करना चाहती हूँ ताकि रणनीतिक दिशा को साझा करने वाले जापान तथा भारत मिलकर हमारी साझेदारी को और आगे बढ़ाया जा सके।

— 高市早苗 (@takaichi_sanae) October 7, 2026

As you mark this milestone, I wish to express my appreciation for the friendship you have extended to Dominica and the generosity shown to our people. I value the bond between our nations and look forward to building on it in the years ahead.

On behalf of the Government and people of Dominica, and personally, I wish you good health, strength and continued success in your service to the people of India."
